Activities Description: - After Finishing your Breakfast, Day full of Exploring Kangeq via Boat. - It takes 1 Hour to travel from Nuuk to Kangeq by Boat. - Kangeq is a former settlement in the Sermersooq municipality in southwestern Greenland. - It was a traditional fishing village, abandoned in the 1980s. The famous artist Aron (1882 - 1869) was born and lived in kangeq. - He was a sealer and painter and is famous for his descriptions of Greenland's culture and people as well as his illustrations of Greenlandic myths and stories. - It is quite an experience walking around this small abandoned ghost town. - Therefore it is almost like a museum that provides insights into the consequences of the politics in the 1950s and 1960s where inhabitants were forced to leave their homes and settle in the "big" and noisy cities. Cellular Jail: After lunch, visit the famous Cellular Jail, which holds a significant place in India's freedom struggle. Many notable freedom fighters were imprisoned here. This three - story prison, constructed by the British in 1906, has been declared a national memorial and is a pilgrimage destination for freedom fighters. This colossal edifice has silently witnessed the most treacherous inhumane atrocities endured by the convicts, who were mostly freedom fighters. Andaman is known for its beaches, and in the evening, you will be taken to one of the most enjoyable beaches in the islands. Corbyn's Cove Beach: Located 8 km away from Port Blair city, Corbyn's Cove Beach is fringed by swaying coconut trees and is famous for its sparkling blue water. The stunning view of the beach against the emerald water is simply breathtaking and refreshing. In addition to its surreal beauty, the island offers various water adventures such as water scooters, jet skiing, parasailing, and boating. Around the beach, there are many stalls serving delightful snacks. (1943) Flag Hoisting Point: This site commemorates Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose, who hoisted the Indian Tricolor Flag on free Indian soil before the island was declared free from British rule. Our Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Flag Point at an altitude of 150 feet in Port Blair, which has now become a source of pride for the island. The Flag Point (Tiranga Point): Located in Port Blair, the capital city of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, this site is another feather in the cap of the islands and its residents. This Indian Union territory has a rich history of freedom fighters and the era of pre - independent India. Numerous historical events took place in the Andamans that are still remembered and treasured. If you are a history buff, including this in your travel itinerary would be a great idea. Light and Sound Show at Cellular Jail: In the evening, proceed to attend the enthralling Sound and Light Show at Cellular Jail, which narrates the saga of countless martyrs of the Indian independence struggle. The show, conducted on the premises of Cellular Jail, provides a brief overview of the events that occurred in the jail prior to India's independence. In the late evening, return to your hotel for a comfortable overnight stay. Note: In case the Light and Sound Show at Cellular Jail is canceled due to weather or maintenance conditions, efforts will be made to arrange alternate sightseeing and to reschedule the show at another time during the itinerary, only if time permits.

Radhanagar Beach is one of the most popular beaches in the Andaman Islands due to its pristine white sand and crystal - clear waters. While here, you can either relax on the silky sand flanking the turquoise blue water or enjoy snacks from various cafes offering local and global cuisine. With its mesmerizing sunsets and sunrises, this beach is a must - visit for all beach lovers. Kalapathar Beach: This is a small, quaint beach in Kalapathar Village, Swaraj Dweep. It features silky golden sands, blue waters, and lush green trees. This beach is not a very popular destination and is often secluded, as there are no water sports activities available here. The path to the beach is beautiful, offering glimpses of the stunning coastline. The beach gets its name from the numerous black rocks present in the water and on the shore. Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island (Ross Island): Originally named after Captain Daniel Ross, this tiny island is located in the South Andaman District, Port Blair, just five kilometers from the Water Sports Complex. It is one of the easiest inter - island visits during your trip to the Andaman Islands. While most tourist spots in the Andamans are popular for their beaches, Ross Island is also known for its historical significance. First occupied in 1782, a sanatorium was built on the island, which the British used as an administrative headquarters for a total of 85 years. Various important government offices were established on this penal settlement during that time. However, after an earthquake in 1941, these structures were abandoned. North Bay Island: From the Water Sports Complex, take a boat to see underwater marine life and various types of corals at North Bay (snorkeling and glass bottom boat rides available at an extra cost). North Bay Beach is not just a place for relaxation but also a hub for water sports. Activities include glass boat rides, sea walking, snorkeling, and scuba diving, allowing you to experience the underwater marine life. A visit to North Bay Island can take up about half of your day. It is advisable to carry snacks, although some snacks (a few standard Chinese dishes and pakoras) and beverages (tea and coffee) are available on the beach.

Cellular Jail: After lunch, we will visit the famous Cellular Jail, which holds a significant place in India's freedom struggle. Many prominent freedom fighters were imprisoned here. This three - story prison, constructed by the British in 1906, has been declared a national memorial and is a pilgrimage destination for freedom fighters. This colossal edifice has silently witnessed the most treacherous inhumane atrocities endured by the convicts, who were mostly freedom fighters. Corbyn's Cove Beach: Located 8 km from Port Blair city, Corbyn's Cove Beach is fringed by swaying coconut trees and is famous for its sparkling blue water. The breathtaking view of the beach against the emerald water is refreshing. In addition to its surreal beauty, the island offers various water adventures such as water scooters, jet skiing, parasailing, and boating. Around the beach, there are many stalls serving delightful snacks. (1943) Flag Hoisting Point: This site commemorates Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose, who hoisted the Indian Tricolor Flag on free Indian soil before the island was declared free from British rule. Our Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Flag Point at an altitude of 150 feet in Port Blair, which has now become a source of pride for the island. The Flag Point (Tiranga Point) in Port Blair, the capital city of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, is another feather in the cap of the islands and its residents. This Indian Union Territory is witness to a rich history of freedom fighters and the era of pre - independent India. Numerous historical events took place in the Andamans that are still remembered and treasured. If you are a history buff, including this in your travel itinerary would be a great idea. Light and Sound Show at Cellular Jail: In the evening, we will attend the enthralling Sound and Light Show at Cellular Jail, which narrates the saga of countless martyrs of the Indian independence struggle. The show, conducted on the premises of Cellular Jail, provides a brief overview of the events that occurred in the jail prior to India's independence. Late in the evening, we will return to your hotel for a comfortable overnight stay. Note: In case the Light and Sound Show at Cellular Jail is canceled due to weather or maintenance conditions, efforts will be made to arrange alternate sightseeing and to reschedule the show for another time during the itinerary, only if time permits.

Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island): Swaraj Dweep, often known as Havelock, is one of the most beautiful and largest islands of the Ritchies Archipelago, a tranquil paradise like no other. Situated 57 km northeast of the South Andamans with an area of 92 sq km, it offers breathtaking nature expeditions. This picturesque island, with its beautiful sandy beaches and lush green forests, is also rated as the seventh most beautiful island in the world. It hosts the world's most renowned beaches, Vijay Nagar Beach and Radhanagar Beach. Spend the day relaxing on these beaches before proceeding to your selected resort. Stay overnight amidst sandy beaches and lush green forests in a comfortable resort. Radhanagar Beach: This beach, situated on the south coast of Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island), is lined with lush coconut trees. Radhanagar Beach is one of the most popular beaches in the Andaman Islands due to its pristine white sand and crystal - clear waters. While here, you can either relax on the silky sand by the turquoise blue water or enjoy various cafes offering local and global snacks. With its mesmerizing sunsets and sunrises, this beach is a must - visit for all beach lovers. Overnight stay at Port Blair. Cellular Jail: After lunch, we will visit the famous Cellular Jail, which holds a significant place in India's freedom struggle. Many notable freedom fighters were imprisoned here. This three - story prison, constructed by the British in 1906, has been declared a national memorial and is a pilgrimage destination for freedom fighters. This colossal edifice has silently witnessed the most treacherous inhumane atrocities endured by the convicts, who were mostly freedom fighters. Corbyn's Cove Beach: Located 8 km away from Port Blair city, Corbyn's Cove Beach is fringed by swaying coconut trees and is famous for its sparkling blue water. The stunning view of the beach against the emerald water is simply breathtaking and refreshing. In addition to its surreal beauty, the island offers various water adventures such as water scooters, jet skiing, parasailing, and boating. Around the beach, there are many stalls serving delightful snacks. (1943) Flag Hoisting Point: This site commemorates Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose, who hoisted the Indian Tricolor Flag on free Indian soil before the island was declared free from British rule. Our Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Flag Point at an altitude of 150 feet in Port Blair, which has now become a source of pride for the island. The Flag Point (Tiranga Point) in Port Blair, the capital city of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, is another highlight for the islands and its residents. This Indian Union Territory is witness to a rich history of freedom fighters and the era of pre - independent India. Numerous historical events took place in the Andamans that are still remembered and treasured. If you are a history buff, including this in your travel itinerary would be a great idea. Light and Sound Show at Cellular Jail: In the evening, we will attend the enthralling Sound and Light Show at Cellular Jail, which narrates the saga of countless martyrs of the Indian independence struggle. The show, conducted on the premises of Cellular Jail, provides a brief overview of the events that occurred in the jail prior to India's independence. In the late evening, we will return to your hotel for a comfortable overnight stay. Overnight stay at Port Blair. Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island (Ross Island): Originally named after Captain Daniel Ross, this tiny island is located in the South Andaman District, Port Blair. It is just five kilometers from the Water Sports Complex and is one of the easiest inter - island visits during your trip to the Andaman Islands. While most tourist spots in the Andamans are popular for their beaches, Ross Island is known for its historical significance. First occupied in 1782, a sanatorium was built on the island. The British used it as an administrative headquarters for a total of 85 years, establishing various important government offices on this penal settlement. However, after an earthquake in 1941, these structures were abandoned. North Bay Island: Travel from the Water Sports Complex by boat to see underwater marine life and various types of corals at North Bay (snorkeling and glass bottom boat rides available at an extra cost). The island offers a breathtaking array of nature expeditions and is rated as the seventh most beautiful island in the world. It hosts the world's most renowned beaches, Vijay Nagar Beach and Radhanagar Beach. Spend the day relaxing on these beaches before proceeding to your selected resort for an overnight stay amidst sandy beaches and lush green forests. Kalapathar Beach: Kalapathar Beach is a small, quaint beach located in Kalapathar Village, Swaraj Dweep. It features silky golden sands, blue waters, and lush green trees. This beach is not a very popular destination and remains secluded most of the time due to the absence of water sports activities. The path to the beach is beautiful, offering glimpses of the stunning coastline. The beach gets its name from the numerous black rocks present in the water and on the shore. Radhanagar Beach: Situated on the south coast of Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island) and lined with lush coconut trees, Radhanagar Beach is one of the most popular beaches in the Andaman Islands due to its pristine white sand and crystal - clear waters. Visitors can relax on the silky sand beside the turquoise blue water. The beach features various cafes where you can enjoy local and global snacks. With its mesmerizing sunsets and sunrises, this beach is a must - visit for all beach lovers. Return to the hotel in the evening for an overnight stay. Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island): Neil is a tiny but beautiful island located 37 km south of the Andaman Islands. With unexplored coral reefs, brilliant biodiversity, white sandy beaches, and tropical forests, it is one of the top tourist spots in the Andamans. The island, with its relaxed vibes and long, deserted beaches, is a perfect place to unwind after the bustle of Havelock. The widest part of the island is about 5 km in length, and you can walk the entire island in about two hours. Natural Rock Formation (Howrah Bridge): The Howrah Bridge, a live natural coral formation resembling a bridge, is also known as the natural bridge. It is an ideal place for photography, especially during sunset when the horizon changes color, attracting many tourists. Bharatpur Beach: Bharatpur Beach is the main destination for most visitors to Neil Island. The greenery and vast sandy beach are a soothing sight. Visitors love the colorful coral reefs and the beautiful aquatic creatures swimming around, adding to the beach's charm. Natural Rock Formation (Howrah Bridge): Neil's famous attraction is the natural bridge formation, locally known as the Howrah Bridge. To see this natural wonder, one must visit the rocky beach No. 2 at low tide, when it is possible to walk on the dead corals and rocks to reach the attraction. For some, the sea creatures found here can be fascinating. You can spot small fish, sea urchins, sea cucumbers, and starfish, and in some areas, you can even see colorful corals slowly growing again. The rocky surface can be slippery in some parts, and many areas are sharp, so caution is advised while walking. Laxmanpur Beach: The secluded Laxmanpur Beach lies 2 km north of the Neil jetty and is considered the sunset point for visitors. This pristine beach offers a beautiful view of the sunset and is a picturesque waterfront covering a vast area of Laxmanpur village. The beach is adorned with a blanket of white shells over the sand, contrasting with the blue sea. It is abundant with many reefs and seashells, which are often collected by visitors as souvenirs.

CELLULAR JAIL: The Cellular Jail, declared a National Memorial, is located in Port Blair. It stands as a mute witness to the brutal atrocities meted out to national freedom fighters who were incarcerated here. Completed in 1906, the jail acquired the name 'Cellular' because it was entirely made up of individual cells for solitary confinement. Originally, it was a seven - block structure with three stories and a central tower acting as its fulcrum, comprising honeycomb - like corridors. This jail, now a place of pilgrimage for all freedom - loving people, draws visitors down memory lane to the years of the freedom struggle. The Jail Museum is open from 9:00 AM to 12:00 noon and from 1:30 PM to 4:45 PM. LIGHT AND SOUND SHOW: The Light and Sound show at the Cellular Jail narrates the saga of the Indian freedom struggle, brought to life through sound and light effects that depict the brutal atrocities faced by freedom fighters deported to these islands and incarcerated in the small cells of this jail. This show is very popular among tourists visiting the islands. Overnight stay at Port Blair.

Activities Description: After breakfast, proceed for sightseeing in Trivandrum, a city named after the Holy Ananth, the cosmic serpent with a thousand heads. Start by visiting Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple, which is 260 years old and the city's most religious icon, built by the Travancore Royal family. The deity, Padmanabha, reclines on the sacred serpent Anantha and is made from over 10, 000 salagramam (sacred stones) brought from Nepal by elephants. Next, visit Puthe Maliga Palace Museum (ticket price extra), a 200 - year - old palace featuring carved wooden ceilings, marble sculptures, and imported Belgian glass. The museum showcases Kathakali images, an armory, portraits of maharajas, ornate thrones, and other artifacts. Later, visit Veli Tourist Village, a popular picnic spot known for its peaceful serenity, where the lake meets the Arabian Sea. The main attractions are the floating bridge and the floating restaurant, which serves a variety of delicious dishes. By evening, proceed to Shankumugham Beach, famous for its breathtaking sunset views. A beautiful mermaid sculpture, over 35 meters long, is a major attraction at this beach. Later, return to Kovalam for an overnight stay.

Activities Description: Breakfast, then proceed to Tala Kaveri, the origin of the river Cauvery, located on the eastern slopes of Brahmagiri peak at an altitude of 1, 350 meters. Trekking in the Brahmagiri hills offers breathtaking views of the hill ranges and is excellent for photography. The steps leading up the hills are steep but climbable. Later, visit Bhagamandala, situated at the confluence of two rivers, the Cauvery and the Kanika. A third river, the Sujyothi, is said to join from underground. Visit the temple dedicated to Bhagandeshwara (Lord Shiva) and receive the blessings of the lord. Coffee Estate Walk + Tasting Experience Post - lunch, visit Abbey Falls, located 8 km from Madikeri town. Abbey Falls is situated amidst coffee plantations and spice estates. It is one of the best waterfalls in the Coorg region, cascading down rocky slopes from a height of 70 feet into a pool. A hanging bridge has been built across the gorge, providing visitors with a beautiful view of the falls. A Kali Mata temple on the other side of the bridge is also worth visiting. The path leading to the waterfalls is filled with thick vegetation, offering a wonderful experience (for those who did not visit the previous day). Madikeri Fort (closed on Mondays) - Preserving its old charm, Madikeri Fort is one of the most famous historical landmarks located in Coorg. An excellent example of spectacular architectural design and construction styles, the fort also houses the Madikeri Fort Museum and the Kote Maha Ganapathi Temple. The elevated structures of the fort provide panoramic views of the town, which are undoubtedly breathtaking and beautiful. Sri Omkareshwar Temple - The Omkareshwara Temple is an ancient shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva, situated in the town of Madikeri. The specialty of the temple is its construction, which reflects a mix of Gothic and Islamic styles. Raja's Seat - The Raja's Seat, meaning the "Seat of Kings, " is a brick and mortar structure with four pillars. It is a popular viewpoint located within a splendid garden of seasonal flowers and musical fountains. The best times to visit Raja's Seat are during the early morning and evening hours to witness breathtaking views of the sunrise and sunset. There is also a toy train attraction for children to enjoy a spectacular view of the mountains. Later, proceed to the hotel and relax. Overnight stay at the Coorg hotel. Extras: You can add: River Rafting Water Trekking Mandalpatti Viewpoint - Jeep Safari (extra cost approx. Rs 2, 000 - 2, 500; Duration approx. 1.5 to 2 hours) Safari Timing: Morning: 6:00 AM - 11:00 AM Evening: 3:30 PM - 6:30 PM Best Time: Sunrise (6 - 8 AM) - Clear views with less crowd. Sunset (5 - 6:30 PM) - Most demanded slot.

Activities Description: After breakfast, enjoy a full - day tour to Ooty and Coonoor, the jewels of the fascinating Nilgiri Hills. These two hill stations are located merely 20 km apart and can be visited in the same day. Morning visit:Sim's Park - Located at a height of 1780 meters, Sim's Park is a botanical garden established in 1874. It features more than 1000 species of flora, including Queensland Kauri Pine, Rudraksha (the bead tree), and various ornamental trees, making it a worthwhile destination. Enjoy long, peaceful walks through the lush greenery and vibrant flowers, as well as opportunities for boating and photography. Lamb's Rock - Situated on the way to Dolphin's Nose in Ooty, Lamb's Rock, also known as Echo Rock, is a popular picnic spot that offers an admirable view of the Coimbatore Plains and the surrounding lush greenery. The route to this location provides trekking opportunities as well. Dolphin's Nose - Located 10 km from Coonoor, Dolphin's Nose is a peak that offers enchanting views of the Nilgiri Hills and Catherine Falls. The peak resembles the nose of a dolphin, hence its name. Botanical Garden - A vast expanse of lawn resembling a golf course, sloping steeply uphill with a variety of trees and shrubs, as well as some conservatories housing exotic ferns and flowering plants. The highlight of this park is the fossilized tree from the prehistoric era, preserved as a natural exhibit. According to carbon dating, it is approximately 20 million years old. Rose Garden - The largest rose garden in India, showcasing more than 20, 000 varieties of roses collected from different parts of the world. Unusual colors, including black and green roses, can also be found. Enjoy a spectacular view of the entire Ooty from the Rose Garden. Catherine Falls Pykara Lake and Waterfall In the evening, proceed to Emerald Lake, an artificial lake and one of the famous tourist spots in Ooty. Enjoy boating, cycling, photography, and a mini toy train ride (available on a direct payment basis). Indulge in shopping around Ooty Lake for chocolates, shawls, eucalyptus oil, and more. Later, return to the hotel and relax. Overnight stay at the Ooty hotel.

Activities Description: Morning after breakfast, we take you for a day of sightseeing in Trivandrum. Trivandrum is an ancient city with a tradition dating back to 1000 BC. Thiruvananthapuram became the capital of the Raja of Travancore in 1750. The name is derived from 'Tiru Ananta Puram', meaning the abode of the sacred serpent Ananta, upon whose coils Vishnu lies in the main temple. It is a peaceful and attractive city built across seven hills. The city's old quarter clusters around the temple, while along the busy Mahatma Gandhi Road are colonial mansions, churches, and modern high - rises. Thiruvananthapuram has managed to retain some of the characteristic ambience of Kerala, such as red - tiled roofs, narrow winding lanes, and intimate corner cafes. Visit the following attractions: The Napier Museum Kuthiramalika Museum Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple In the afternoon, go to the beach for relaxation. Return to the hotel; the rest of the day is free at leisure. Overnight stay at Hotel Kovalam.

CELLULAR JAIL: The Cellular Jail, declared a National Memorial, is located in Port Blair and has stood as a mute witness to the brutal atrocities meted out to national freedom fighters who were incarcerated here. Completed in 1906, the jail acquired the name 'Cellular' because it was entirely made up of individual cells for solitary confinement. Originally a seven - block structure with three stories and a central tower acting as its fulcrum, it comprises honeycomb - like corridors. This jail, now a place of pilgrimage for all freedom - loving people, draws visitors down memory lane to the years of the freedom struggle. The Jail Museum is open from 9:00 AM to 12:00 noon and from 1:30 PM to 4:45 PM. LIGHT AND SOUND MUSIC SHOW: The Light and Sound show at the Cellular Jail narrates the saga of the Indian freedom struggle, brought to life through sound and light effects depicting the brutal atrocities inflicted on the freedom fighters deported to these islands and incarcerated in the small cells of this jail. This show is very popular among tourists visiting these islands. Overnight stay at Port Blair.

Activities Description: Breakfast at hotel. Enjoy a fulfilling sightseeing tour in North Goa with us, exploring the beautiful, famous sandy beaches up to the top of fortresses and forts that protected the land from naval attacks.We start with the ancient Fort Aguada, which was built in 1612. This fortress serves as a defensive structure against invaders from the seas, equipped with a lighthouse and was constructed near the Sinquerim Beach. The fort was constructed by the Portuguese to defend against Dutch attacks and is complete with a freshwater spring, which was how the fort got the name "Aguada, " which means watery in Portuguese. The lighthouse was built later, in 1864, and is now the oldest of its kind in Asia.Then we'll hit the trio Baga - Calangute - Candolim beaches, starting from the closest, Sinquerim Beach. Walk down the fort and enjoy the picturesque view from Sinquerim beach, best known as the most scenic shores among tourists on top of being located near the ancient Aguada Fort. We slowly make our way to Calangute Beach where one can enjoy a range of fun activities and shop to their heart's content. You can also shop for beach necessities, take part in water activities, or enjoy the food and snacks here. It is also the longest beach in North Goa that stretches from Candolim to Baga. As we continue walking the shore, we'll reach Baga Beach, where one can find the most hill rocks amongst the three beaches. It is also the most famous for the commercial nightlife with many famous bars, lounges, and clubs here. We move next to Anjuna Beach where you'll be stunned by the beautiful scenery as palm trees adorn the white sandy beach while the unique red laterite rocks and black rock formations juts out from the sea. It's also the preferred beach for water sports and to shop at the market.Finally, we'll visit Vagator Beach, which is located on the northernmost tip of Bardez Taluka. This beautiful beach is known for its soft, white sandy beach with granite cliffs and offers a series of water activities as well. But this doesn't mean you can't just lie down and enjoy the tranquil waves and serene atmosphere. You can also explore the Chapora Fort nearby, a tower that was erected on the Chapora River by Muslim ruler Shahpura. Take in the unforgettable view of the beach and bask under the sunlight as you watch the sunset from this rare spot.Overnight in Goa at your appointed hotel.

Activities Description: After breakfast, we start our full - day South Goa tour with Shree Mangesh Temple, also called Shri Manguesh Temple, located within Mangeshi Village of Goa. This gorgeous 400 - year - old temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva, who is worshipped in the form of Lord Mahueshi. Legends say that Lord Shiva, who lost everything to Parvati over a game of dice, came to Goa and disguised himself as a Tiger. He coincidentally scared Parvati, who then asked to be rescued, and Lord Shiva transformed back to his original form and followed her back. The name Manguesh came from Parvati, who spoke "Mam Grisha" when asking for help.Goa is known for its serious of churches and convents of Old Goa. You don't want to miss the famous Basilica of Bom Jesus, a church from the 1600s and the most popular church of Old Goa. It is within the UNESCO World Heritage Site and remains an iconic landmark in Goa. Bom Jesus means "Good/Baby Jesus" As you enter the Jesuit church, you'll see what remains some well - preserved remains of baroque architecture brought in by the Portuguese, earning it a place in the Seven Wonders of Portuguese Origin in the World. We'll also visit the Church of Our Lady, which is a Gothic - style church first built in 1541 on a hill that overlooks Panjim. The imposing design is credited to a famed architect of his time, Antoni Gaudí. Initially built as a chapel, it became a parish in 1600 before a major construction took place in 1609, turning it into the church we know today. In the 18th century, the iconic symmetrical zigzag stairs were added and finally, Goa's second - largest bell tower was built in 1871. Then we move to where Goa's largest bell is located, the Sé Catedral de Santa Catarina, a cathedral built to celebrate the Portuguese victory over a Muslim army in 1510 before capturing Old Goa on the day of the feast of Saint Catherine. The construction finished in 1619 since it began in 1562 and houses some of the most historically valuable artworks, paintings, sculptures, and the Chapel of the Cross of Miracles. It is said that a vision of Christ appeared on the year the construction finished.If you have been dying to shop in Goa, then you'll love Panjim Market, the haven of shopping lovers for local products, souvenirs, snacks, and anything you want in Goa. Take home something of Goa from here and maybe along with gifts to share with your loved ones back home.But if being in the crowd has been draining your energy, you'll appreciate the quiet surrounding Dona Paul Beach has to offer. Named after a woman of charity in Portuguese India, Dona Paula Amaral Antónia de Souto Maior, the villagers of Dona Paula renamed their village with hers to honor her memory after her contribution to improve the village's quality of life. Today, people love to visit the beach which is only visited during peak seasons and is considerably sparse of people otherwise. Enjoy the gorgeous view of Mormugao Harbour, a major trading port of India since 1963, as vessels make their way in and out after exporting iron ores that reach 27.33 million tons a year.Miramar Beach of Goa is another stunning place you don't want to miss. It used to be called the Gasper Dias Beach and is a hotspot for hangout or take part in watersport activities. Restaurants and bars can also be seen lining up near the beach with a great nightlife aspect as people join the beach party where famous Goan drinks and foods are served.Spice up your trip with Mandovi River Cruise at an extra cost. For around one hour, you'll be taken on a ride on luxurious cruise through the Mandovi River and with the sunset as your backdrop. There is live DJ music, traditional dance performances in the Carnival Village before boarding.Overnight at hotel.

Rohtang Pass (51 km from Manali)A gateway to Lahaul & Spiti Valley, Rohtang Pass (altitude 3, 980 meters) is one of the most spectacular spots in Himachal Pradesh. Beyond Rohtang, you can witness the stunning Sonapani Glacier and the twin peaks of Gaypan, known for their serene beauty. Nearby lies the sacred Beas Kund, the origin of the Beas River, believed to be the meditation site of Sage Vyas, making it both a spiritual and scenic destination.

Aru Valley - Located around 11 km from Pahalgam, Aru Valley is the base camp for trekking to the Kolhoi Glacier and the Tarsar - Marsar Lake. Aru lies beside the Aru River and is known for its scenic meadows and activities like horse riding, hiking, and trekking. Chandanwari - Chandanwari, located 15 km from Pahalgam, is the starting point of the famous Amarnath Yatra. It is breathtaking and surrounded by snow - dusted mountains and the Lidder River flowing by. Chandanwari is famous for snow sledding on a snow bridge and enjoying a picnic. Baisaran - Baisaran is a beautiful destination 6 kms away from Pahalgam. It is also called the mini Switzerland of India, with tranquil meadows, pristine lakes, and picturesque settings. You can stroll down the area or sit down to have a picnic. Baisaran also offers activities like pony rides, zorbing, etc. Betaab Valley - Betaab Valley is a breathtaking combination of picturesque surroundings encircled by tall deodar trees and pine forests, with the Lidder River flowing right through it. It got its name from the Bollywood movie Betaab, starring Sunny Deol and Amrita Singh, which was shot here. After sightseeing back to the hotel. Dinner & overnight stay at hotel.

Activities Description: The name "Doodpathri" means Valley of Milk. It is said that the famous saint of Kashmir, Sheikh Ul Aalam (Sheikh Noor Din Noorani), prayed here. While searching for water in the meadows to offer prayers, he pricked the ground with his stick, and milk came out. He remarked that the milk could only be used for drinking and not for performing ablution. Upon hearing this, the milk immediately changed its state to water, and the meadow was named Doodpathri. The water currently flowing through the meadows has a milky appearance from a distance and remains very cold throughout the year. The lush green grasses over the vast meadows and the silver shining streams running over large stones further enhance its beauty. Doodpathri features sloping grassy landscapes with a diversity of multi - colored flowers up to Chang. The famous Tosamaidan lies to the west of Doodpathri. Doodpathri is situated in a bowl - shaped valley in the Pir Panjal Range of the Himalayas, at an altitude of 2, 730 m (8, 957 ft) above sea level. It is an alpine valley covered with snow - clad mountains and meadows of pine, fir, and deodar. The natural meadows, which are covered with snow in winter, allow the growth of wildflowers such as daisies, forget - me - nots, and buttercups during spring and summer. After that, return to the hotel for a hot delicious dinner and stay overnight .

Mata Kheer Bhawani Temple: - The temple of Kheer Bhawani is situated at a distance of 14 miles east of Srinagar against the background of natural sight near the village of Tula Mula. The temple of Ragnya Devi is called "Kheer Bhawani" because numerous devotees offer milk and kheer (Indian sweet dish) to the sacred spring. It is believed that milk and kheer turn to black color to warn of any impending disaster. Manasbal Lake: - Manasbal Lake is located about 30 km north of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir State. It has predominantly rural surroundings with three villages, Kondabal, Jarokbal and Gratbal overlooking the lake. Manasbal is considered as the 'supreme gem of all Kashmir lakes' with lotus (Nelumbo nucifera) nowhere more abundant or beautiful than on the margins of this lake during July and August. It is the deepest lake of Kashmir valley and perhaps the only one that develops stable summer stratification. Hari Parbat Temple - Hari Parbat (SHARIKA PEETH) is situated at the periphery of Srinagar city is an ancient and one of the holiest place of Kashmir. It is the abode of Maha Shakti. The Divine mother of Shri Jagat Amaba Sharika Bagwati also known as Maha TRIPURSUNDHARI OR RAJESHWARI locally called HARIE. The EIGHTEEN ARMED goddess SHARIKA is regarded as the presiding deity (ISHT - DEVI) of Srinagar city.The Goddess Sharika is represented by a Sayambhu "SRI CHAKRA" (Mahamaha Srichakra) also called "MAHA SRIYANTRA" which consists of circular Mystic impressions and triangular patterns with fot(Bindhu) at the centre. The mystic SHRICHAKAR self - engraved on a vertical holy rock (shilia) is located at the middle of western face of Hari Parbat (Hillrock).

Originally called 'Gaurimarg' by shepherds, its present name was given in the 16th century by Sultan Yusuf Shah, who was inspired by the sight of its grassy slopes emblazoned with wild flowers. Gulmarg was a favourite haunt of Emperor Jehangir who once collected 21 different varieties of flowers from here. Today Gulmarg is not merely a mountain resort of exceptional beauty - it also has the highest green golf course in the world, at an altitude of 2, 650 m, and is the country's premier ski resort in the winter.

About Verinag - One of the largest springs in India, Verinag, is easily accessible through a bye pass from the Jammu - Srinagar high way. Verinag is named after Nila Nag, the son of the wise saint, Kashyap Rishi, who reclaimed the Kashmir valley, the original shape of this spring was in the circular form of a kund which was later developed into octagonal shape by Jehangir. A Shaivite shrine just outside the complex draws pilgrims every year, who come for a ritual dip in the spring of the first day of the year according to the lunar Hindu calendar.

The journey can be extended to Gauri Kund, located at the base of Mount Adi Kailash, but only if health permits, as it is situated near 5, 000 meters and may lead to Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS). Solang Nala (Valley): Solang Nala (Valley) derives its name from a combination of the words Solang (a nearby village) and Nullah (water stream). It is a side valley at the top of the Kullu Valley in Himachal Pradesh, India, located 14 km northwest of the resort town of Manali on the way to Rohtang Pass. Solang Valley is known for its summer and winter sports conditions. The most commonly offered sports include parachuting, paragliding, skating, and zorbing. Snow melts during the summer months starting in May, and skiing is then replaced by zorbing (a giant ball that accommodates 2 people, rolled down a 200 - meter hill), paragliding, parachuting, and horse riding. A ropeway was recently opened, and reaching the summit can be accomplished by ATVs, ropeway, or climbing (trekking). Activities Description: Today morning, after breakfast, we will proceed to visit Auli for sightseeing. Auli is a popular skiing destination in India, known for its glittering slopes and clean environment. Dotted with apple orchards, oaks, and deodars, Auli is a charming hill town with numerous ski resorts situated amidst the Himalaya range. Activities Description: In the morning, have breakfast at the hotel. After breakfast, proceed for the Vrindavan sightseeing. One of the oldest cities on the banks of the Yamuna, Vrindavan is considered one of the most important pilgrimage sites for devotees of Krishna. It is said that Lord Krishna spent his childhood in Vrindavan. The name of the city is derived from "Vrinda" (meaning basil) and "van" (meaning grove), which may refer to the two small groves at Nidhivan and Seva Kunj. Since Vrindavan is considered a sacred place, many people come here to abandon their worldly lives. Banke Bihari Mandir: Shri Banke Bihari Mandir is a Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Krishna. This temple is among the seven temples of Thakur of Vrindavan. The image of Lord Krishna in the temple appears in the form of a child and is seen standing in the Tribhanga position. Radha Vallabh Temple: Situated near Gotam Nagar on the cliff near Bankey Bihari temple, Radha Vallabh Mandir is one of the seven temples of Thakur of Vrindavan. This temple epitomizes the sacred and divine love of Radha and Krishna, displayed in the rarest form known as 'Ras - bhakti'. Enshrined by Lord Krishna, the temple does not have a deity of Radha. Instead, it has a crown placed next to Lord Krishna to signify her presence. Radha Raman Temple: Built by Gopala Bhatta Gosvami, this temple was established in 1542. It is said that the deity here is self - manifested from one of the shalagram - shilas. As an idol of Radha is not present here, a crown placed near Lord Krishna depicts her. Nidhivan: Nidhivan, a temple nestled in the holy birthplace of Krishna, has a sense of miracle attached to it. Nidhivan is known as the place where Lord Krishna visits every night to perform Ras Leela. ISKCON Vrindavan: Located in the Raman Reti area of Vrindavan, the ISKCON temple has become a major attraction. Also known as Sri Sri Krishna Balaram Mandir, the temple is dedicated to Lord Krishna and Balram. Prem Mandir: Known as the "Temple of God's Love, " Prem Mandir is one of the most popular places to visit in Vrindavan. It is dedicated to Radha Krishna as well as Sita Ram. Made out of white marble and adorned with intricate carvings, this temple is also famous for its architectural beauty. After sightseeing, return to Mathura. Overnight stay at the Mathura hotel.

Agra Fort: Also known as Lal Qila, Fort Rouge, or the Red Fort of Agra, the Agra Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage site. It is situated about 2.5 km northwest of the famous Taj Mahal. The construction of the massive fort of red sandstone by the banks of the Yamuna River was started by Emperor Akbar. After sightseeing, proceed to Delhi. The capital of India, Delhi is a cosmopolitan city with a historic Old Delhi and modern New Delhi. From historical monuments to crowded shopping malls, and from an extensive network of the modern metro system to the Delhi University campus, Delhi has multiple personalities and is considered to be a city with a heart. The narrow, winding lanes and bylanes of Old Delhi are a testament to the former Mughal rule. Old Delhi houses one of the country's oldest and busiest markets - Chandni Chowk. There is a big parking issue so the driver will go back other palace if his contact no. in not working then you have to arrange a taxi or wait for your driver & send a message any other driver.Kedarnath: The Kedarnath shrine, one of the 12 jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva, is a scenic spot situated against the backdrop of the majestic Kedarnath range. Kedar is another name of Lord Shiva. According to legend, the Pandavas after having won over the Kaurava in the Kurukshetra war, felt guilty of having killed their own brothers and sought the blessings of Lord Shiva for redemption. He eluded them repeatedly and while fleeing took refuge at Kedarnath in the form of a bull. On being followed he dived into the ground, leaving his hump on the surface. The remaining portions of Lord Shiva appeared at four other places and are worshipped there as his manifestations. The arms appeared at Tungnath, the face at Rudranath, the belly at Madhmaheshwar and his locks (hair) with head at Kalpeshwar. Kedarnath and the four above - mentioned shrines are treated as Panch Kedar.Kedarnath Weather - Due to its high altitude the weather in Kedarnath remains cold for most part of the year. Badrinath, one of the 'Ancient Four Dhams, ' is one of the most celebrated pilgrimage spots of the country and is situated at an elevation of 3, 133 meters, guarded on either side by the two mountain ranges known as Nar & Narayan with the towering Neelkanth Peak providing a splendid backdrop. This revered spot was once carpeted with wild berries. Thus the place got the name "Badri van", meaning "forest of berries".Tapt Kund: Natural thermal springs on the bank of the river Alaknanda, where it is customary to bath before entering the Badrinath temple.Mana Village: Inhabited by an Indo - Mongolian tribe, it is the last Indian village before Tibet. Is motorable upto Mana.Bhim Pul: On the other side of Mana village, a massive rock forming a natural bridge lies over the Saraswati River. It presents a spectacular view of water thundering down through the narrow passage under the rock. It is believed to have been placed there by Bhim, the second eldest among the five Pandava brothers.Vyas Gufa(cave): Near Mana Village, this is a rock cave where Ved Vyas is believed to have composed the Mahabharata and the Pauranic commentaries.Badrinath The average maximum temperature will be around 18° Celsius, and the average minimum is 8° Celsius. Activities Description: On your arrival in Delhi, you will be met by a representative and transferred to a hotel. Delhi was the capital of Indraprastha and capital of the Pandavas in the course of the Mahabharata. Your morning tour begins with old Delhi, built by way of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in 1639 AD. You'll visit the Raj Ghat where the father of India, Mahatma Gandhi was cremated. For Indians, it is a place where our national spirit peaks, and for tourists, it's a great opportunity to look at the Indian Nationalistic spirit up close and personal. You will be touring the museum that was built to commemorate him. You will pass by Chandni Chowk, an extremely famous and busy market in vintage Delhi. You'll enjoy India up close and see the locals and their bustling day - to - day activities. Chandni Chowk has shops selling delicious mouth - watering meals, garments, jewels, family matters, etc. This is definitely a shopper's paradise. Continuing the historic Delhi monument tour we will visit the Jama Masjid, one of the iconic, historic and largest mosques in India - constructed by Shah Jahan. In the afternoon, you will visit Qutub Minar, India's largest Minaret. Qutub Minar, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was built in 1192 by way of Turk ruler Qutb - Ud - Din Aibak. This area is beautiful, and very scenic, bustling with people and activities. You will then visit Humayun's tomb, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This place is very alive, historically touching and very beautiful. Your next stop is India Gate, constructed in reminiscence of the martyred soldiers. You will then pass through the Parliament House, President's House and Government Secretarial Buildings. You will continue the tour visiting Lakshmi Narayan Temple, a temple dedicated to Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Narayan.

Return to the hotel for dinner and an overnight stay.

Activities Description: Today morning, after breakfast, we leave for Solang Valley. Solang Valley is an activity hub located 15 kilometers northwest of Manali Town. Here, guests can enjoy paragliding, zorbing, skiing, and cable car rides. Other leisure activities, such as horse riding and photography, are attractions that keep guests engaged. On the way to Solang Valley, we will visit Him Valley Fun Park, one of the first amusement and cultural parks situated at an altitude of about 7, 000 feet above sea level. After the fun park, we will cross the Beas River to visit Vashisth Village, which is well known for its hot springs. There is an old temple dedicated to the sage Vashisth and to Lord Rama, believed to be more than 4, 000 years old. We will also visit Nehru Kund. After breakfast, we will proceed to local sightseeing, starting with the Hadimba Devi Temple. This cave temple was built in 1553 by Maharaja Bahadur Singh and features a superbly crafted four - tiered pagoda roof. It is famous for its exquisitely carved doorway. Next, we will move to the Club House, which has comprehensive facilities that include a roller skating rink, an auditorium, billiards rooms, a library, a bar, and a restaurant, making it a wonderful outing for the day. Adventurous souls can also try their hand at zip - lining, where one must cross a river using a ropeway. Next, we will visit the Tibetan Monastery and Van Vihar, both located near the famous Mall Road of Manali and Old Manali. After covering the sightseeing, we will head to our pre - booked hotel in Manali for dinner and an overnight stay.

Tibetan - Monastery (0.5 Kms) - This Gadhan Thekchoking Gompa dominates the Tibetan area around the bottom of the Mall in Manali. The Tibetan refugees built the Gompa in the late 1969. The main attraction of the monastery is the handicrafts of Tibetan artistry and the carpets that are woven and sold in the monastery. Club House (2 Kms from Mall) - Located on the left bank of Manalsu Nallah. Club house is famous for a amusement activities like skating, Disco Theque etc. Club house is surrounded by various picnic spots, Later in the evening free to explore the Shopping Malls (Mall Road & IBEX Market) of Manali

Besides, the valley is also known to be a good site for camping. Instead of taking the regular pony ride it is recommended that tourists explore the surrounding valley on foot to get a full sense of its beauty. Betaab Valley Located on the way to Chandanwari, the valley was named Betaab after the Bollywood movie by the same name! Earlier known as Hajan Valley, after the release of the movie, it was renamed as major part of the movie was shot here. Set amid picture perfect environs complete with snowcapped mountains, gurgling streams, colorful willow trees & the warm sun; making it an ideal for an artist's canvas! The valley is a walk - able distance from Pahalgam. The crystal clear & chilly water of the stream bubbling down from the snowy hills is a delight; locals here drink this water too. Baisaran and Tulian Lake are few nearby attractions that can be visited. Chandanwari Pahalgam to Chandanwari is easily accessible by taxi. Activities Description: Visit Conifer, where mountains and snow - covered peaks are illuminated by golden sun rays against a blue sky, and the shaded valley of the Lidder River forms the identity of Aru. Aru is a popular hill station in the trans - Himalayan region, characterized by a vast grassland surrounded by a narrow valley or ravine on one side. The blooming nature amidst a cool climate makes the still and serene Aru one of the most beautiful hill resorts in Kashmir. Like all other hilly areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Aru offers a wonderful view of water reservoirs and mountains. The most beautiful aspect of Aru lies in the small village houses made of wood and stone. Aru is the perfect destination to take a break from the pollution, dust, and stress of city life, situated at an altitude of 2, 708 meters and 15 km from Pahalgam. Chandanwari is the starting point of the Amarnath Yatra, which takes place every year in the month of Sawan (Rain). Chandanwari is famous for snow sledging on a snow bridge. The Sheeshnag River at Chandanwari captivates visitors with its sheer force and clear waters. Visitors have the opportunity to go sledge riding and ascend to some heights, up to the fifth point, which is also a route that yatris take to reach the Amarnath Cave. "Snow fights" are a common activity here before people sledge back down. Many prefer to sip a cup of tea or snack at the nearby dhabas. Betaab Valley (4 km) is the location where the famous movie "Betaab" was filmed. Ponies can be hired to explore the stream and forest, which are bound by many popular trees. The way to Chandanwari from Pahalgam features an idyllic spot for a picnic. Filmgoers will recognize this area instantly, as it has been the location for several movie scenes. The natural meadows of Gulmarg, covered with snow in winter, allow the growth of wildflowers such as daisies, forget - me - nots, and buttercups during spring and summer. The meadows are interspersed with enclosed parks and small lakes, surrounded by forests of green pine and fir. The Gulmarg Gondola is a tourist attraction in itself and is one of the highest cable cars in the world. It features a two - stage ropeway: The first stage transfers passengers from the Gulmarg resort at 2, 600 m (8, 530 ft) to Kongdoori Station at 3, 080 m. The second stage of the ropeway, which has 36 cabins and 18 towers, takes skiers to a height of 3, 950 m (12, 959 ft) on Kongdoori Mountain, a shoulder of nearby Apharwat Peak (4, 200 m or 13, 780 ft). Gulmarg also has a famous ski resort and boasts the world's highest 18 - hole golf course.

If his contact number is not working, you will need to arrange another taxi or wait for your driver and send a message through any other driver.Kedarnath: The Kedarnath shrine, one of the 12 jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva, is a scenic spot situated against the backdrop of the majestic Kedarnath range. Kedar is another name for Lord Shiva. According to legend, after having won over the Kauravas in the Kurukshetra war, the Pandavas felt guilty about having killed their brothers and sought the blessings of Lord Shiva for redemption. He eluded them repeatedly and, while fleeing, took refuge at Kedarnath in the form of a bull. On being followed, he dived into the ground, leaving his hump on the surface. The remaining portions of Lord Shiva appeared at four other places and are worshipped there as his manifestations. The arms appeared at Tungnath, the face at Rudranath, the belly at Madhmaheshwar, and his locks (hair) with the head at Kalpeshwar. Kedarnath and the four above - mentioned shrines are treated as Panch Kedar.Kedarnath Weather - Due to its high altitude, the weather in Kedarnath remains cold for most of the year. Summer here is cool and pleasant, while winter is severe. During the summer season, the temperature varies around 20° Celsius. Light woolen wear is recommended. After that depart for Tabo Tabo, home to one of the most significant gompas, not only in Spiti but in the entire Tibetan Buddhist world. Tabo holds the distinction of being the largest monastic complex in Spiti, constructed in 996 AD. Visit Dhankar Monastery, the traditional capital of Spiti, which sits prettily on a hilltop. Today, more than 160 Lamas reside here. The main attraction of this monastery, which is over 7 centuries old, is the statue of Dhyan Buddha, where four complete figures of Buddha sit back to back. Enjoy dinner and an overnight stay in Tabo.

Activities Description: Post breakfast, we drive to Nubra Valley. The road journey from Leh to Nubra Valley passes over Khardung La (the highest motorable road in the world) at 5, 602 meters (18, 390 feet), approximately 39 km from Leh. From the pass, one can see south over the Indus Valley to seemingly endless peaks and ridges of the Zanskar range, and north to the giants of the Saser massif. Nubra Valley is popularly known as Ldumra, or the valley of flowers. It is situated in the north of Ladakh, between the Karakoram and Ladakh ranges of the Himalayas. The average altitude of the valley is 10, 000 feet above sea level. Upon arrival in Nubra, we check in at our camp or hotel. In the evening, we drive to Hunder, where you have the opportunity to ride on a Bactrian camel (double - humped) amidst the sand dunes of this high - altitude desert, with snowcapped mountains on the horizon. Between Hunder and Diskit, you will come across sand dunes beside the road. In isolation, you could easily be among the sand dunes of the Thar Desert in Rajasthan. Enjoy a half - day tour of the world - famous Mughal Gardens, including: Nishat Garden: Located on the bank of Dal Lake, with the Zaberwan Mountains as its backdrop, Nishat Bagh offers a magnificent view of the lake beneath the snowcapped Pir Panjal mountain range. The garden was designed and built in 1633 by Asif Khan, the elder brother of Nur Jehan. Shalimar Garden: The Shalimar Bagh is the celebrated royal garden of Kashmir. Emperor Jahangir was so fascinated with the garden that he referred to it as "one of the sights of Kashmir." Shalimar Bagh is located on the northeast side of Dal Lake, approximately fifteen kilometers from the center of Srinagar. It was laid out by Jahangir as Farah Baksh ("the delightful") in 1619 while he was founding the city of Srinagar. Cheshma Shahi: Also known as the royal spring, Cheshma Shahi is one of the Mughal gardens built around a spring by Ali Mardan, a governor of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan, in 1632. The garden is located in the Zaberwan Range, near Rajbhawan (Governor's house), overlooking Dal Lake in Srinagar, Kashmir. In the late evening, enjoy a Shikara ride on Dal Lake for up to 1 hour. Dinner and overnight stay in Srinagar at Hotel 5 Falcone.

Dinner and overnight stay at the hotel.

Activities Description: After breakfast in the morning, we will begin our countryside day trip to Gulmarg, located at 2, 440 meters above sea level. Gulmarg is one of the most beautiful hill stations, also known as the "Meadows of Flowers." The drive past colorful villages and rice fields provides insight into the rich cultural history of Kashmir. We will arrive at the small picturesque market town of Tangmarg and continue on a scenic drive of 14 kilometers to Gulmarg. Gulmarg features one of the best ski slopes in the world and the highest golf course with 18 holes. We will arrive in Gulmarg early in the afternoon and begin a short tour around the meadow to familiarize ourselves with its beauty. In Gulmarg, we will have the option to board the Gondola cable car system and ascend towards the Afarwatt Mountain range. The 8 - minute ropeway ride will take you past colorful shepherds to the lower ridge of the Afarwatt peak. From this vantage point, you can capture numerous photos of the nearby mountain ranges that stand tall like sentinels guarding the rich natural beauty of the Kashmir valley. In the evening, we will drive back to Srinagar and check into a houseboat. After refreshments, we will take a 1 - hour Shikara ride on Dal Lake. This boat ride glides you past wonderful floating vegetable gardens, handicraft centers, and the inherited lifestyle of people living on the lake for decades. The evening is free for personal activities such as shopping, followed by an overnight stay at the houseboat.

Activities Description: After a leisurely breakfast, begin your half - day city tour visiting the following attractions: Hidimbi Devi Temple Manu Temple Vashisht Temple Tibetan Monastery Van Vihar near Mall Road Hidimbi Devi Temple, also known as the Dhungri Temple, is located 2 km from the Manali Bus Stand. This ancient cave temple was built in 1553 by Raja Bahadur Singh and is dedicated to Hidimbi Devi, the wife of Bhima, one of the Pandavas from the Mahabharata epic. The Hidimbi Devi Temple stands 24 meters tall and features three square roofs with timber tiles, surmounted by a cone - shaped fourth roof covered in brass. The wooden facade and windows of the temple are richly carved, and the wooden door frame is adorned with carvings of various deities and other designs. The walls of the temple are uniquely decorated with horns of animals, and the base is made of whitewashed mud - covered stonework. Manu Temple, dedicated to the Indian sage Manu, is located in Old Manali. Manali is named after the sage Manu, who is considered the creator of the human race on Earth according to mythology, and it is believed that he meditated here. This is thought to be the only temple of Manu in India. Manu Temple was built in the pagoda style of architecture. To reach the temple, one must walk through the slippery stone paths of Old Manali for about 200 meters. This ancient temple is a prominent place of worship for the local people of Manali, who visit daily to offer their prayers to the sage Manu. Vashisht Temple in Manali is dedicated to Sage Vashisht, the Kula Guru of Lord Rama, located in the village of Vashisht across the River Beas. The village of Vashisht was named after Rishi Vashisht, one of the seven sages of Hinduism. The Vashisht Temple is believed to be more than 4000 years old. The Vashisht Hot Water Spring is one of the famous attractions in this region, believed to have medicinal value. The springs are said to cure many skin diseases, and many people visit the Vashisht baths to take a dip and rid themselves of skin infections and ailments. Evening free for independent activities or exploring Mall Road. Overnight stay at a Manali hotel.

The drive takes you past the Abdullah Bridge, which connects the banks of the Jhelum River, snaking its way towards the northwestern frontier of Kashmir. Proceed for local sightseeing in Srinagar, which includes: Mughal Gardens: Nishat Bagh (the Garden of Spring) Shalimar Bagh Botanical Garden Floating Gardens Chashma Shahi (the Royal Fountains) Temples and Shrines: Shankaracharya Temple Hazratbal Shrine Tulip Garden Shankaracharya Temple: The Shankaracharya Temple, also known as the Zyesteshwara Temple or Sulaiman Throne (Takht e Sulaiman), is located at a height of 1, 000 feet (300 m) above the plain and overlooks the city of Srinagar. Nishat Bagh: Nishat Bagh is a terraced Mughal Garden built on the eastern side of Dal Lake, close to Srinagar in the state of Jammu and Kashmir, India. It is the largest Mughal Garden in the Kashmir Valley. The name 'Nishat Bagh' is Urdu for "Garden of Joy, " "Garden of Gladness, " and "Garden of Delight." Shalimar Bagh: Shalimar Bagh is a Mughal Garden in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, India, linked through a channel to the northeast of Dal Lake. It is also known as Shalimar Gardens, Farah Baksh, and Faiz Baksh. Construction of the gardens began in 1641 during the reign of Emperor Shah Jahan and was completed in 1642. Chashme Shahi Garden: Chashme Shahi, also called Chashma i Shahi, is one of the Mughal gardens built in 1632 AD around a spring by Ali Mardan Khan, a governor of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan, as a gift for his elder son, Prince Dara Shikoh. Tulip Garden: The Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden, previously known as the Model Floriculture Center, is located in Srinagar, in the Indian union territory of Jammu and Kashmir. It is the largest tulip garden in Asia, covering an area of about 30 hectares (74 acres). Situated at the base of the Zabarwan range, it is built on sloping ground in a terraced fashion consisting of seven terraces with an overview of Dal Lake. The tulip garden is home to around 75 varieties of tulips, as well as 46 varieties of flowers, including hyacinths, daffodils, and ranunculus, which were also brought from Holland. Tulsi Manas Mandir is dedicated to Lord Rama and named after the saint poet Tulsi Das. It displays the Shikhara style of architecture and features various inscriptions from the Ram Charit Manas on the walls of the temple. Bharat Mata Mandir is a unique shrine dedicated to our country, Mother India. The temple has no deities, only a relief map of the country carved in marble. The temple was conceived by Babu Shiv Prasad Gupta, a freedom fighter. It was built in 1936 and inaugurated by Mahatma Gandhi, making it the only temple in the world dedicated to a country. Durga Temple is located near the Durga Ghat on the bank of the River Ganga. Built in the 18th century, it houses an imposing idol of Goddess Durga and is one of the main temples in Varanasi. Tulsi Manas Mandir is dedicated to Lord Rama and named after the saint poet Tulsi Das. It displays the Shikhara style of architecture and exhibits various inscriptions from the Ram Charit Manas on the walls of the temple. Bharat Mata Mandir is a unique shrine dedicated to our country, Mother India. The temple has no deities, only a relief map of the country carved in marble. The temple was the brainchild of Babu Shiv Prasad Gupta, a freedom fighter. It was built in 1936 and inaugurated by Mahatma Gandhi, and has since been the only one in the world dedicated to a country. Durga Temple, located near the Durga Ghat on the bank of the River Ganga, was built in the 18th century. It houses an imposing idol of Goddess Durga and is one of the main temples in Varanasi. Activities Description: Mawlynnong (4906 ft / 1496 m, 80 km / approximately 3 to 4 hours drive one way) Dawki Lake (5904 ft / 1800 m, 30 km / approximately 1 to 2 hours drive) After breakfast, drive to Mawlynnong - "Asia's Cleanest Village & God's Own Garden." Mawlynnong offers many interesting sights, such as the living root bridge and the unique natural phenomenon of a boulder balancing on a smaller rock. After visiting the village, drive to Dawki and explore the border area. Drive back to Shillong for an overnight stay. Mawlynnong village is located about 100 km ahead of Shillong on the Shillong - Dawki Road, 30 km from Pynursla. The village consists of 75 households with a population of 400. This idyllic location epitomizes a standard that all other villages should aspire to achieve. Dubbed the cleanest village in India by Discover India Magazine, the primary village school, which goes up to class V, boasts a no - dropout record and a literacy rate of 90%. Paved walkways and beautiful flowerbeds mark the village, while waterfalls, a living root bridge, hilly rivulets, acacia plantations, and an excellent view of the distant plains of Bangladesh contribute to the village's ambiance. The primary economic activities of the village include farming betel nut and leaves, broomsticks, and pepper, along with bee rearing. The village headman takes responsibility for ensuring visitors' comfort, providing insight into the life of the Khasis, the influence of the Church, and the village's transformation.

Activities Description: Morning city sightseeing tour of Jaisalmer. Visit Jaisalmer Fort, located on Trikuta Hill; this fort is the largest and most beautiful landmark of the city. The fort is home to shops, stalls, and various business establishments. Also known as Sonar Quila or the Golden Fort, it rises from the sand and merges with the golden hues of the desert ambiance. The Jain temple, situated inside the fort and built between the 12th and 15th centuries, showcases Rajasthan's unique artistry. Explore the havelis, mansions built by wealthy merchants, which are still in excellent condition. The intricate craftsmanship of the havelis is unparalleled. Havelis such as Patwon - ki - Haveli and Salim - Singh - ki - Haveli are remarkable for their exclusive cutwork, yellow and red stone treatment, and bracket - shaped decoration of peacocks. The rich merchants, inspired by the classic style of the royals, constructed large mansions (havelis) adjacent to each other, reflecting medieval culture with profusely decorated walls and ceilings, as well as intricately carved exteriors and interiors. In the afternoon, visit the Khuri Sand Dunes and a typical Rajasthani desert village. Take a camel ride to view the sunset from the dunes, using the same camels for the safari to get acquainted with them, as the sky is set ablaze. This can be an unforgettable experience. Overnight stay in Jaisalmer.

Chandanwari - Chandanwari, located 15 km from Pahalgam, is the starting point of the famous Amarnath Yatra. It is breathtaking and surrounded by snow - dusted mountains and the Lidder River flowing by. Chandanwari is famous for snow sledding on a snow bridge and enjoying a picnic. Baisaran - Baisaran is a beautiful destination 6 kms away from Pahalgam. It is also called the mini Switzerland of India, with tranquil meadows, pristine lakes, and picturesque settings. You can stroll down the area or sit down for a picnic. Baisaran also offers activities like pony rides, zorbing, etc. Betaab Valley - Betaab Valley is a breathtaking combination of picturesque surroundings encircled by tall deodar trees and pine forests, with the Lidder River flowing right through it. It got its name from the Bollywood movie Betaab starring Sunny Deol and Amrita Singh, which was shot here. After sightseeing back to the hotel. Dinner & overnight stay at hotel.

The Giza Pyramid Complex: The Giza Pyramid Complex is the most significant part of ancient Egyptian civilization, dating back more than 4, 000 years. It consists of three main pyramids, six smaller pyramids, the Sphinx, and the Valley Temple. The Valley of the Kings: This site features the most important tombs of the kings from the New Kingdom period (1570 - 1070 BC). It contains 63 tombs adorned with magnificent decorations of pharaohs such as Ramses I, II, III, IV, V, VI, VII, IX, X, Amenophis I, Hatshepsut, and Tutankhamun (the most visited tomb in the Valley). The Valley of the Kings was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979. The Temple of Hatshepsut: Known as "Djeser Djeseru, " meaning the holy sanctuary, this majestic temple was built for one of ancient Egypt's most powerful pharaohs, Queen Hatshepsut. Constructed in 1479 BC during the New Kingdom, it took 15 years to complete and was dedicated to the god Amun - Ra, serving as her mortuary temple. The Colossi of Memnon: These two colossal statues, carved from sandstone, stand 18 meters high and weigh 720 tons each, depicting Pharaoh Amenophis III (1386 - 1350 BC). Damaged by an earthquake in 27 BC, they were restored in 199 AD. The Colossi gained fame during Greco - Roman times for the sounds they produced at dawn. Karnak Temple: Known as "Pr Imn, " meaning the house of Amun, this is one of the largest temple complexes in the world. It contains sanctuaries for several gods, including Osiris, Isis, and Ptah, but is primarily dedicated to the Theban triad of Amun, Mut, and Khonsu. Activities Description: Day 3 is the centrepiece of this Andaman kayaking package. The morning session is the mangrove channel paddle - the interior side of Havelock Island has mangrove waterways that narrow into shallow forest channels where the motorboats that carry most island visitors cannot enter. The kayak moves at paddle pace through sections of the channel where the mangrove root systems are close on both sides and the canopy reduces the light overhead. The guide leads the group through the navigable sections and the pace is slow enough to observe the mangrove ecosystem - the mudskippers on exposed root surfaces, the waterbirds in the canopy, the small fish in the shallow water visible through the hull below. The afternoon session paddles the route to Elephant Beach bay from the island's north side - the same bay that the motorboat reaches in 45 minutes is reachable by kayak in around 1.5 to 2 hours of open water paddling, with the reef visible below in the shallow sections of the approach. Overnight at Havelock.

Activities Description: The chartered boat departs from Port Blair early in the morning for Barren Island, which is approximately 135 kilometers northeast across the open Andaman Sea. The crossing takes around 6 to 8 hours, depending on sea conditions. Barren Island is the only confirmed active volcano in South Asia, and the island is uninhabited. No landing is permitted; the boat approaches and circles the island, allowing views of the black lava coastline, the caldera rim, and the crater from the water. Dolphins are commonly sighted during the open ocean run to the northeast, and the crossing itself passes through waters that are home to several cetacean species. The volcanic ecosystem at Barren Island, characterized by the lava coastline, the crater structure, and the absence of terrestrial life found on other Andaman islands, represents a unique ecology found nowhere else in this archipelago and in this part of Asia. Seabirds utilize the thermal updrafts around the island. The return crossing brings the group back to Port Blair by late evening as part of this Andaman wildlife package, which includes an overnight stay in Port Blair.

Activities Description: After an early breakfast, you will drive to visit the high - altitude lake known as Shonga - tser Lake, popularly referred to as Madhuri Lake, located 35 km away from Tawang near the China border. The drive to Sangestser Lake is thrilling, and you can still see the war bunkers that were used during the Chinese aggression in 1962. Nestled amidst pristine mountains and picturesque surroundings, the lake was formed in the aftermath of the 1950 earthquake. Prior to the earthquake, this area was used as grazing ground for cattle, as evidenced by the protruding trunks of dead trees in the middle of the lake. The lake is supervised by Army personnel, who have also arranged for a nearby cafeteria. Tourists can enjoy delicious momos and Maggi, topped off with a cup of tasty coffee or tea. Visitors can also trek around the lake while enjoying the gentle breeze. You can drive further to Bumla Pass, located about 37 km away from Tawang at the Indo - China border, over 15, 200 ft above sea level. On the return journey, take a photo stop at the beautiful PTSO Lake, located 17 km away from Tawang, also known as Pangong Tang Tso Lake, which offers an extremely scenic drive with a bird's eye view of the township below. Later in the afternoon, drive back to the hotel. The rest of the evening is at leisure, with an overnight stay at the hotel.

The city is renowned for having the best riding camels in the world. The 600 - year - old temple is dedicated to Karni Mata, an incarnation of Goddess Durga. The temple hosts thousands of rats, which are considered sacred and worshipped accordingly. Be very careful while entering the inner sanctum, as it is believed that if you accidentally step on a rat, a gold replica must be made to compensate for the lost life. Set on the shores of Lake Pichola and surrounded by hills, Udaipur grew in complete contrast to the harsh deserts of the rest of Rajasthan. As the capital of the old Mewar State, it was the only Rajput stronghold to uphold its Hindu allegiance in the face of Muslim invasion. Activities Description: After breakfast, we proceed for a full day of local sightseeing in Gangtok as part of your Darjeeling Sikkim package tour. The first stop is Tashi View Point, which offers panoramic views of Mt. Kanchenjunga and the surrounding Himalayan range on a clear day. The sight of the world?s third highest peak glowing in the morning sun is breathtaking and highlights why this Darjeeling Sikkim package tour is so popular among women travelers. From Tashi View Point, we visit Ganesh Tok, a small hilltop temple dedicated to Lord Ganesha, featuring a viewing gallery that provides a 360 - degree view of Gangtok city below. Next, we drive to Hanuman Tok, a sacred temple surrounded by dense forest and prayer flags. The peaceful atmosphere and the views from this elevation make it one of the hidden gems of Gangtok. We then visit Banjhakri Falls, a beautiful waterfall set within a themed park featuring tribal sculptures and gardens. The cascade of water through the rocky terrain is a refreshing sight, and the park is perfect for photographs. The themed statues tell stories from Sikkimese folklore, and the energy of the waterfall creates a calming effect that many women on this Darjeeling Sikkim package tour find deeply rejuvenating. The afternoon takes us to Do Drul Chorten, one of the most important Buddhist stupas in Sikkim, surrounded by 108 prayer wheels that devotees spin as they walk around the stupa. This meditative practice is deeply calming and offers a glimpse into the Buddhist spiritual culture that defines Sikkim. Next, we visit the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, which houses a rare collection of Tibetan manuscripts, statues, thangka paintings, and religious artifacts. Our final stop is the Enchey Monastery, a 200 - year - old monastery that provides deep insight into Sikkimese culture and Buddhism. The monastery?s peaceful courtyard, colorful murals, and spinning prayer wheels create a meditative atmosphere that many people on this Darjeeling Sikkim package tour find profoundly peaceful. The evening is at leisure for shopping and café hopping at MG Marg. Try the local craft beer at one of the rooftop cafés, browse the bookshops for titles on Himalayan culture and Buddhism, or simply sit at a window seat and watch the clouds drift across the mountains as the streetlights come on. MG Marg has a charm that is hard to find anywhere else in India ? clean, safe, pedestrian - friendly, and surrounded by mountain views in every direction. Overnight stay in Gangtok.

Activities Description: After an early breakfast, we proceed to one of the most exciting excursions of your Darjeeling Sikkim package tour ? a visit to Tsomgo (Changu) Lake. The drive from Gangtok to Tsomgo takes about 2 hours and climbs steeply through dense forests of rhododendron and pine. As the altitude increases, the vegetation changes dramatically from lush green trees to barren rocky slopes dusted with snow. The road itself is an adventure, with sharp hairpin turns and military checkpoints along the way. Tsomgo Lake sits at an altitude of 12, 400 feet, surrounded by snow - clad mountains and steep rocky slopes. This stop on your Darjeeling Sikkim package tour is one of the most photographed locations in all of Sikkim. The lake changes color with the seasons deep blue in summer, frozen white in winter, and emerald green during the monsoon. The stillness of the water, the snow on the surrounding peaks, and the crisp mountain air create a scene that feels like a painting come to life. Yak rides are available at the lake for an additional personal cost, and many women enjoy riding the gentle yaks along the lakeshore for photographs. From Tsomgo, we continue to Nathula Pass, located on the Indo - China border at 14, 140 feet. This visit is subject to permit availability and weather conditions. Nathula is one of the few places in India where you can stand at the actual border with China, see the Chinese soldiers on the other side, and feel a powerful rush of patriotism. The views from Nathula are stunning snow - covered peaks, barbed wire fencing, and the Indian flag fluttering proudly in the icy wind. A small canteen at the pass serves hot samosas, Maggi, and chai that taste heavenly in the freezing cold. This stop at Nathula is a once - in - a - lifetime experience. The experience at Nathula is deeply emotional for many women on this Darjeeling Sikkim package tour. Standing at 14, 000 feet, at the very edge of the nation, surrounded by the silence of the mountains and the courage of Indian soldiers, is something that stays with you long after the trip ends. Many women in the group find themselves quietly emotional, proud, and grateful. We return to Gangtok by evening along the same scenic route, giving you time to rest and warm up before a hot dinner at the hotel. The day's experiences from the frozen beauty of Tsomgo Lake to the patriotic energy of Nathula make this one of the most memorable days of your Darjeeling Sikkim package tour. Sit with your fellow travelers over dinner and share the moments that moved you the most. These shared stories are what make a journey so special. Overnight stay at Gangtok.
