Activities Description: After breakfast, we check out from the Gangtok hotel and begin the scenic drive to Darjeeling, the Queen of the Hills. This Darjeeling Sikkim package tour drive takes approximately 4 to 5 hours, and the route offers some of the most stunning mountain roads in the Eastern Himalayas. You will pass through lush tea estates that blanket the hillsides in every shade of green, small mountain villages where life moves at its own gentle pace, and viewpoints where the entire Himalayan range stretches across the horizon. The road descends from Gangtok into the Teesta Valley before climbing again toward Darjeeling, creating a journey that feels like a roller coaster through paradise. Upon arrival in Darjeeling, we check into the hotel. The first thing you notice about Darjeeling is its colonial charm ? the Victorian architecture, the narrow winding streets, and the mist that rolls in and out of the town like a living curtain. This Darjeeling Sikkim package tour now enters its most romantic and nostalgic phase. The town has a magical quality that is hard to describe until you experience it yourself. Every corner reveals a new view, a hidden café, or a colonial - era building with a story to tell. The famous toy train whistle echoes through the valley, adding to the old - world charm. The evening is free for you to explore Mall Road and Chowrasta, the main gathering point in Darjeeling. This open square is surrounded by heritage buildings, bookshops, and tea rooms. Local vendors sell roasted corn, churpi (dried cheese), momos, and hot chocolate. Ponies are available for short rides around the square, and children and adults alike enjoy feeding the flocks of pigeons that gather at Chowrasta every evening. The vibe is relaxed and friendly, and you will see families, couples, and fellow travelers all enjoying the mountain air together. Walk along the Ridge, enjoy a cup of world - famous Darjeeling tea at one of the heritage tea rooms, and watch the sunset light up the Kanchenjunga range in shades of gold and pink. Street performers sometimes play the guitar or flute in the evening, adding a musical touch to the mountain air. If you are a reader, the Oxford Book Store at Chowrasta is a must - visit ? the collection of books on Himalayan history, Buddhism, and travel writing is exceptional. This evening on your Darjeeling Sikkim package tour is all about soaking in the charm of a hill town that has captivated travelers for over a century. Overnight stay at Darjeeling.

Activities Description: Wake up very early today for the highlight of your Darjeeling Sikkim package tour ? the sunrise at Tiger Hill. We drive to Tiger Hill in the pre - dawn darkness, wrapped in warm jackets and carrying hot flasks of tea. The road climbs through thick fog and pine forests, and the anticipation builds with every turn. As the sky slowly transitions from black to deep blue to orange, the first rays of sunlight illuminate the peak of Mt. Kanchenjunga, causing the entire mountain to glow golden against the dark sky. On exceptionally clear mornings, you can also see Mt. Everest in the far distance, a tiny white triangle peeking above the clouds on the Nepal border. The sunrise at Tiger Hill is one of those life moments that changes you. Many people on this Darjeeling Sikkim package tour describe it as the most beautiful thing they have ever witnessed. The crowd falls silent as the first golden rays touch Kanchenjunga, and for a few magical minutes, time stands still. After sunrise, we visit the Ghoom Monastery en route, one of the oldest and most sacred Buddhist monasteries in Darjeeling, housing a magnificent statue of Maitreya Buddha. We also stop at Batasia Loop, where the famous Darjeeling Himalayan Railway toy train makes a figure - eight turn around a beautiful war memorial garden with Kanchenjunga as the backdrop. After returning to the hotel for breakfast, we continue our Darjeeling Sikkim package tour sightseeing with visits to the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute, which chronicles the history of mountaineering in the region with exhibits on famous expeditions, including the first successful Everest summit. The museum displays actual equipment used by climbers, route maps, and photographs that bring the stories to life. Right next door is the Padmaja Naidu Zoological Park, home to the rare Red Panda, Snow Leopard, and Tibetan Wolf. The zoo is set on a hillside, and the walking paths through forested enclosures make it a pleasant experience. We also visit Tenzing Rock, a natural rock face named after the legendary Tenzing Norgay, who practiced climbing here as a young man. A visit to a famous tea garden follows, where you can see the entire tea - plucking and processing process up close and taste fresh Darjeeling tea straight from the source. The aroma of freshly processed tea leaves is something you will not find anywhere else in the world. Our final sightseeing stop is the Japanese Temple, known for its peaceful ambiance and beautiful architecture that blends Japanese and Himalayan styles. The evening is free for shopping and café hopping in Darjeeling. Pick up boxes of premium Darjeeling tea, woolen shawls, handmade jewelry, and Tibetan artifacts from the local shops. Nathmulls and Golden Tips are two legendary tea shops where you can sample and buy some of the finest teas in the world. The narrow lanes around Chowrasta are filled with tiny shops selling everything from hand - knit sweaters to Buddhist singing bowls. This full day on your Darjeeling Sikkim package tour perfectly balances natural beauty, cultural exploration, and personal leisure. It is the kind of day that reminds you why travel is the best gift you can give yourself. Overnight stay at Darjeeling.

Activities Description: After breakfast, drive to visit Saheliyon - Ki - Bari, or 'Garden of the Maids' in English. This garden was built by Maharana Bhopal Singh for a group of 48 young women attendants who accompanied a princess to Udaipur as part of her dowry. Saheliyon - Ki - Bari features lush greenery, flowers, beautiful fountains, lotus pools, and marble artifacts and pavilions, offering splendid views and creating an ideal romantic setting. Drive past Queen's Resort and Sukhadia Circle. Visit Bhartiya Lok Kala Museum, which showcases a rich collection of folk dresses, ornaments, puppets, masks, and dolls. Next, visit the City Palace, a palace complex built by Maharana Udai Singh. The City Palace is grandeur personified, consisting of several buildings with towers, balconies, and cupolas. The City Palace houses a crystal gallery that boasts royal artifacts and the world's largest private collection of crystal. It is one of Rajasthan's largest palaces and offers splendid views of Lake Pichola. A must - not - miss experience in Udaipur is the hour - long Mewar Sound and Light Show, which takes place every evening at the City Palace complex and regalizes the history of Mewar. Visit Jagdish Temple, built by Maharana Jagat Singh, which is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Explore Gulab Bagh. Overnight stay in Udaipur.

The stream in the upper valley runs through fir and pine forest with the water carrying the particular clarity of a high - elevation stream fed entirely by snowmelt and forest spring rather than agricultural runoff. The forest floor in the upper Doodhganga zone carries the particular density of a belt that has not been subject to the grazing pressure that the Yusmarg meadow receives from the seasonal Gujjar herds - the ground vegetation is thicker and the bird activity in the morning hours is noticeably different from the open meadow below. The vehicle takes the group to the upper limit of the motorable track above Yusmarg and the walk from that point follows the stream for 3 to 5 kilometres into the forest before the return. Overnight at Yusmarg.

Activities Description: Today morning after early breakfast, you will drive to visit high altitude lake called as Shonga - tser Lake, popularly known as Madhuri Lake located 35 kms away from Tawang near the China Border. The drive to Sangestser Lake is full of thrill and one can still see the war bankers that had been used during the Chinese aggression in 1962. Nestled amidst the pristine mountains and picturesque surrounding, it was formed in the aftermath of the 1950 earthquake. Prior to the earthquake, this piece of land used to be employed as the grazing ground for the cattle. The evidence of it can be seen in the protruding trunks of the dead trees from the middle of the lake. The lake has been under supervision of Army men, who have also arranged for a cafeteria nearby. Tourists can relish on the delicious Momos, Maggi‟s topped with a cup of tasty coffee or tea. Tourists can also take to trekking around the lake while enjoying the gentle lashes of the pleasant breeze around. You can drive further to Bumla Pass which is located about 37 km away from Tawang at the Indo - China border over 15, 200 ft above sea level. During return take a photo stop at the beautiful PTSO lake Enroute (17 kms away from Tawang, Pangong Tang Tso Lake popularly known as PT Tso which is an extremely scenic drive with bird's eye view of the township below). Later in the afternoon drive back to hotel. Rest of the evening at leisure overnight at hotel

This bustling pedestrian zone is the social and commercial center of the capital, offering a clear view into the daily lives of the local residents. Walking through the area allows you to browse traditional handicrafts, observe the distinct mountain architecture, and enjoy the crisp evening air without the interference of heavy vehicle traffic. Located at an impressive 13200 feet, this shrine is dedicated to Harbhajan Singh, a soldier who is widely believed to protect the personnel stationed in the border regions. The site is filled with a profound sense of duty and spiritual protection, making it a distinctly unique stop on your circuit. Following the visit, we begin our return journey back toward the city of Gangtok. As you descend through the mountains, you can process the visual experiences of the morning safely.

Activities Description: The third day of your sikkim tour is dedicated to a comprehensive exploration of the capital city and its surrounding cultural landmarks. After a wholesome breakfast at your hotel, we begin the local sightseeing tour designed to showcase the diverse heritage of Gangtok. Our first stop is typically the Flower Show, a vibrant display of the region's rich botanical diversity. This colorful start to the day provides an excellent opportunity for nature photography and a deeper appreciation of the fertile Himalayan environment that surrounds the city limits. Continuing our city tour on this sikkim tour, we proceed to Ganesh Tok, a prominent hilltop temple dedicated to Lord Ganesha. This sacred site is positioned at a high elevation, offering sweeping views of the city layout and the distant mountain ranges. Devotees and travelers alike visit this shrine to seek blessings and tie colorful prayer flags along the pathways. We also visit the Lasha Waterfall and the Bakthang Waterfall, both offering picturesque scenes of cascading mountain water against rocky cliffs. The sound of the rushing water creates a highly restorative atmosphere for all visitors. For expansive panoramic views, your sikkim tour incorporates a dedicated stop at the renowned Tashi View Point. We also visit the Gungjang Monastery, an important center for Tibetan Buddhist practice. Walking through the monastery grounds, you can observe the traditional architecture, intricate murals, and the disciplined daily routines of the resident monks. We conclude the day with a visit to a local plantation, allowing you to learn about the agricultural practices before returning to your comfortable hotel in the city center for a hot dinner and a restful night of sleep.

Activities Description: Start: After breakfast & hotel check - out 09:00 AM - Journey starts for Bishnupur Rasmancha Visit time: 30 - 40 minutes About the spot: Rasmancha is the earliest and most iconic structure of Bishnupur, built in 1600 AD by King Hambir Malla Dev. Unlike typical temples, it was designed as a ceremonial pavilion rather than a shrine. During the annual Ras festival, idols of Radha - Krishna from surrounding temples were brought here and placed on the raised platform for public viewing. Architecturally, it is unique due to its pyramidal roof, arched galleries, and laterite - brick construction, showing a blend of Mughal and Bengali styles. Best for photography in morning light. Shyam Rai Temple Distance: 1.2 km Drive time: 5 - 7 minutes Visit time: 35 - 40 minutes About the spot: Built in 1643 AD, this is a Pancha - ratna (five - towered) temple dedicated to Lord Krishna. It is considered the finest example of Bishnupur terracotta art. The temple walls are covered with intricate terracotta panels depicting: Scenes from Krishna Leela Episodes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata Daily life of 17th - century Bengal Each panel is detailed and expressive, making this temple a visual narrative carved in clay. Jorbangla (Keshto Rai) Temple Distance: 0.6 km Drive time: 3 - 5 minutes Visit time: 30 - 35 minutes About the spot: Built in 1655 AD, Jorbangla is architecturally unique, shaped like two traditional Bengali huts joined together, topped by a single tower. The terracotta work here is bold and dramatic, portraying: Battle scenes Royal processions Mythological stories Social life of medieval Bengal This temple represents the peak of Bishnupur's temple architecture, combining rural Bengali design with royal craftsmanship. Madanmohan Temple Distance: 1.8 km Drive time: 8 - 10 minutes Visit time: 30 - 35 minutes About the spot: Constructed in 1694 AD, this Eka - ratna (single - towered) temple is dedicated to Lord Krishna as Madan Mohan. The temple is known for: Elegant proportions Graceful terracotta panels Calm, spiritual atmosphere Unlike the grand terracotta density of Shyam Rai, Madanmohan offers a more balanced and serene experience, ideal for quiet exploration. Mrinmoyee Temple Distance: 0.8 km Drive time: 3 - 5 minutes Visit time: 20 - 25 minutes About the spot: Mrinmoyee Temple is believed to be the oldest temple in Bishnupur, dating back to 997 AD. Dedicated to Goddess Durga, it is deeply revered by locals. This temple holds special importance during Durga Puja, as Bishnupur follows ancient traditional rituals here, different from modern Kolkata - style celebrations. The temple reflects Bishnupur's living religious heritage, rather than purely architectural grandeur. Bishnupur Archaeological Museum Distance: 1 km Drive time: 5 minutes Visit time: 30 - 40 minutes About the spot: Officially known as Acharya Jogesh Chandra Purakirti Bhawan, this museum preserves the region's archaeological and cultural history. Inside you'll find: Stone sculptures from the 10th - 12th centuries Ancient inscriptions Terracotta fragments Tribal art and folk culture exhibits This museum provides essential historical context to the temples you've just visited. 01:15 - 02:00 PM | Lunch in Bishnupur Ideal areas: Near Rasmancha Station Road area Opt for light Bengali meals to stay energized for travel. Gokulnagar Temple (Last Stop) Distance: 6 - 7 km Drive time: 15 - 20 minutes Visit time: 25 - 30 minutes About the spot: Located beside Lalbandh Lake, Gokulnagar Temple is a laterite stone temple built by the Malla rulers. It stands out for: Peaceful lakeside setting Simpler architectural style Scenic surroundings Because of its location on the outskirts of Bishnupur, it is best visited last before heading toward Kolkata. 03:00 PM - Drive to Kolkata Distance: 135 - 140 km Travel time: 4 - 4.5 hours Expected arrival: 7:00 - 7:30 PM

Activities Description: Morning city sightseeing tour of Jaisalmer. Visit Jaisalmer Fort, located on Trikuta Hill; this fort is the largest and most beautiful landmark of the city. The fort is home to shops, stalls, and various business establishments. Also known as Sonar Quila or the Golden Fort, it rises from the sand and merges with the golden hues of the desert ambiance. The Jain temple, situated inside the fort and built between the 12th and 15th centuries, showcases Rajasthan's unique artistry. Explore the havelis, mansions built by wealthy merchants, which are still in excellent condition. The intricate craftsmanship of the havelis is unparalleled. Havelis such as Patwon - ki - Haveli and Salim - Singh - ki - Haveli are remarkable for their exclusive cutwork, yellow and red stone treatment, and bracket - shaped decoration of peacocks. The rich merchants, inspired by the classic style of the royals, constructed large mansions (havelis) adjacent to each other, reflecting medieval culture with profusely decorated walls and ceilings, as well as intricately carved exteriors and interiors. In the afternoon, visit the Sam Sand Dunes and a typical Rajasthani desert village. Take a camel ride to view the sunset from the dunes, using the same camels for the safari to get acquainted with them, as the sky is set ablaze. This can be an unforgettable experience. Overnight stay in Jaisalmer.

Activities Description: Your Darjeeling journey begins when our representative meets you at NJP Railway Station or Bagdogra Airport. After warm greetings and assistance with your luggage, you will start the mountain drive to Samthar via Fagu and Paparkheti villages. The 85 - kilometer route climbs steadily through diverse landscapes. Tea estates appear first, with their orderly rows covering the hillsides. Workers move between the bushes, plucking leaves that become the region's famous tea. This agricultural backbone supports much of Darjeeling's tourism and local economy. As the altitude increases, forests grow denser, with oak, pine, and rhododendron trees creating a thick canopy overhead. The road winds through these woods, occasionally opening to reveal stunning valley views. Small villages emerge where mountain communities maintain traditional lifestyles, central to authentic Darjeeling tourism experiences. Samthar is tucked away in the Kalimpong district, a peaceful offbeat destination that has escaped mass tourism development. This quiet village offers natural beauty and homestay accommodations. Few travelers venture here, making it perfect for those seeking genuine Darjeeling tourism away from crowded spots. The village is home to about forty families living simple mountain lives. There are no restaurants or shops cluttering the landscape?just homes, fields, and forests. This untouched quality attracts visitors who are tired of commercialized Darjeeling destinations where authenticity is often lost. Samthar's elevation provides pleasant temperatures and clean air. Morning mist often blankets the valleys before the sun burns it away. Evening brings cool breezes and clear skies, perfect for stargazing. These natural rhythms define quality Darjeeling tourism, focusing on a connection with nature rather than attractions. Check into your Samthar homestay upon arrival. The host family greets you with tea?mountain hospitality's universal language. Your room offers basic comforts: clean bedding, an attached bathroom, and simple furniture. Luxury is not the goal here; authentic Darjeeling tourism prioritizes cultural exchange over amenities. Meet your hosts properly during tea time. They will share stories about village life, farming practices, and how their family has lived here for generations. These conversations provide insights into real mountain living that polished Darjeeling tourism packages often overlook. Take an evening walk around Samthar while there is still light. The village is small enough to explore in thirty minutes, but you will want to linger at viewpoints. Mountain ranges stretch across the horizon, their peaks catching the colors of sunset. Photography enthusiasts will find endless subjects to capture the beauty of Darjeeling tourism. As darkness arrives, village routines wind down. Without street lights, you notice the transition acutely. Families light lamps in their homes, and kitchen fires start for dinner preparation. The slowing pace helps visitors decompress from the urban stress that brought them seeking Darjeeling tourism escapes. Stars emerge in spectacular numbers once full darkness settles. The Milky Way stretches overhead, and constellations appear crisp and bright. This celestial show represents one of Darjeeling tourism's underappreciated aspects?the incredible night skies visible from remote mountain villages. Dinner at your homestay features home - cooked mountain food, including dal, rice, seasonal vegetables, and possibly chicken curry. Everything comes from nearby sources?gardens, local markets, and village farms. The meals taste different from restaurant food because they are made with care rather than the commercial efficiency that sometimes plagues mainstream Darjeeling tourism. After dinner, more conversations unfold around the family table or in the sitting room. Your hosts explain seasonal changes, weather patterns, agricultural challenges, and how tourism has impacted their village. These honest discussions provide depth to your understanding of Darjeeling tourism that guidebooks never capture. Sleep comes easily in Samthar. The mountain air, profound quiet, and comfortable tiredness combine to deliver deep rest. You will wake refreshed, ready to continue your Darjeeling tourism adventure through this special region.

If you wake early, step outside to witness the sunrise over the mountain ranges. The peaks catch the first light while the valleys remain shadowed, creating dramatic contrasts that are beloved by Darjeeling photographers. Village morning routines start early here; farmers head toward the fields, women fetch water, and children prepare for school if it is a weekday. Observing these patterns unfold fosters an appreciation for the rhythm of mountain life that sustainable Darjeeling tourism aims to support rather than disrupt. Before breakfast, explore Samthar's surroundings on foot. Trails lead through nearby forests and fields. Your hosts can suggest routes that match your fitness level and available time. Walking these paths connects you with the landscapes that define the natural appeal of Darjeeling tourism. Return to your homestay for breakfast, which includes local bread, eggs, vegetables, butter, honey, and strong tea. Mountain mornings can be chilly, making hot food especially welcome. Your hosts serve generous portions because feeding guests well is important in cultures that support authentic Darjeeling tours. Thank your homestay family properly before departing; they have shared their home, meals, and stories, opening their lives to strangers seeking Darjeeling tourism experiences. Many travelers maintain connections with host families, returning year after year to visit friends rather than just tourist destinations. The drive toward Kalimpong goes through Lava, making it a logical stop. Lava is surrounded by thick forests at a comfortable altitude. The village has a working monastery where monks maintain Buddhist practices that are integral to the regional culture shaping the character of Darjeeling tourism. Stop at the Lava monastery for a visit. This is not a tourist attraction but an active religious site where monks live and pray. Prayer wheels line the exterior, and prayer flags flutter overhead. Inside, butter lamps flicker, incense burns, and murals cover the walls. Respectful visitors are welcome to observe and learn about Buddhism's role in the regions of Darjeeling tourism. If timing permits, you might witness prayer sessions, where monks chant in deep voices, creating resonant sounds. Even without understanding the words or rituals, the atmosphere feels powerful. Cultural immersion like this elevates Darjeeling tourism beyond mere sightseeing into genuine learning experiences. Lava has small restaurants for lunch stops. Momos are universal here?steamed or fried dumplings with various fillings. Each place prepares them slightly differently, and trying different versions becomes a fun food adventure in Darjeeling tourism. Pair them with spicy chutney and hot tea. The forest surrounding Lava deserves exploration if you have time. Trails wind through dense vegetation that hosts diverse bird species. Serious birdwatchers come to Lava specifically for this biodiversity. Even casual nature lovers enjoy the forest atmosphere and fresh air that define quality Darjeeling tourism experiences. Continue driving to Kalimpong, which takes roughly an hour from Lava. The road winds downward slightly as you approach the town, and the landscape opens up with more development visible. Kalimpong is substantially bigger than anywhere you have stayed, though it maintains the hill town character that is important to the appeal of Darjeeling tourism. Check into your Kalimpong hotel in the mid - afternoon. After the homestay basics, the hotel feels luxurious with comfortable beds, reliable hot water, and room service. Both experiences have value when exploring Darjeeling tourism?villages offer authenticity, while towns provide comfort and broader amenities. Late afternoon is perfect for exploring Kalimpong's main market area. The bazaar has shops selling Tibetan handicrafts, woolens, books, and local products. People come from surrounding villages to shop here, making it an excellent place for observing daily life beyond polished presentations of Darjeeling tourism. Kalimpong has decent cafes where you can relax with drinks and snacks; some have balconies overlooking the valleys. Sitting and watching the town's rhythms provides a different perspective on Darjeeling tourism?how communities function, how modernity mixes with tradition, and how tourism impacts local economies. Dinner options vary widely in Kalimpong. Restaurants serve Indian, Chinese, Tibetan, and continental cuisines. After days of simple mountain meals, you might want something different, or you might crave dal and rice because you have developed a taste for it during your Darjeeling tourism journey. The evening in Kalimpong has a pleasant energy. Families stroll along the main roads, young people gather at popular spots, and shops stay open late. It is lively without being overwhelming?a nice balance reflecting how Darjeeling tourism can develop without destroying the qualities that initially attracted visitors.

Next, visit Durpin Monastery, which sits prominently on Durpin Hill. This Buddhist gompa follows the Gelugpa tradition. Inside, you'll find a large Buddha statue, detailed murals, and prayer wheels. The monastery represents the spiritual dimension deeply woven into the Darjeeling tourism regions. Monks at Durpin are usually welcoming to respectful visitors, explaining the monastery's history, daily practices, and Buddhist teachings. These interactions provide cultural depth that elevates Darjeeling tourism from simple vacationing to meaningful learning experiences. The viewpoint near Durpin Monastery rivals Deolo for scenic beauty, offering excellent perspectives of Kalimpong town with mountains in the background. Many consider this essential for understanding how Darjeeling tourism destinations balance development with the preservation of natural beauty. Drive past the army golf course next. Seeing such a well - maintained course at this altitude, surrounded by mountain terrain, highlights an interesting aspect of Kalimpong's colonial history that shaped Darjeeling tourism infrastructure development. Kalimpong's fame extends to its nurseries, which produce exceptional cacti and orchids. Visit several to see the incredible variety. These nurseries have built international reputations, becoming major attractions for plant - loving Darjeeling tourism visitors. The cactus nursery displays hundreds of varieties from around the world, including tiny specimens, huge columnar types, flowering species, and rare collectors' items. Gardeners explain cultivation techniques and how they source different varieties. For plant enthusiasts, this represents a highlight of Darjeeling tourism. Orchid nurseries are equally impressive. Kalimpong's climate suits orchids perfectly, and the varieties grown here are stunning?diverse in colors, sizes, and forms. Learn about propagation methods and conservation efforts. These nurseries demonstrate how Darjeeling tourism can support specialized horticulture while attracting visitors. You can purchase plants if interested; staff will pack them carefully for travel and provide care instructions. Taking home a living memento from your Darjeeling tourism adventure creates a lasting connection to the place. Handicraft centers offer shopping opportunities that support traditional artisans. Watch craftspeople create items using generational techniques, including handmade paper, woven textiles, and wood carvings. Each craft represents cultural heritage that responsible Darjeeling tours help preserve by providing markets for traditional skills. By late afternoon, you've covered Kalimpong's main attractions. Return to your hotel to rest before dinner. The day has been full but well - paced. A quality Darjeeling tour prioritizes experiencing things properly over rushing through checklists. The evening is free time for more market exploration, café visits, or hotel relaxation. Reflect on how this journey has shown different aspects of the Darjeeling tour?remote village immersion, forest monasteries, horticultural excellence, and handicraft traditions. Together, they create a comprehensive understanding of the region's appeal.

The blooming nature amidst a cool climate makes the still and serene Aru one of the most beautiful hill resorts in Kashmir. Like all other hilly areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Aru offers a wonderful view of water reservoirs and mountains. Chandanwari is the starting point of the Amarnath Yatra, which takes place every year in the month of Sawan (Rain). Chandanwari is famous for snow sledging on a snow bridge. The Sheeshnag River at Chandanwari captivates visitors with its sheer force and clear waters. Visitors have the opportunity to go sledge riding and ascend to some heights, up to the fifth point, which is also a route that yatris take to reach the Amarnath Cave. "Snow fights" are a common activity here before people sledge back down. Many prefer to sip a cup of tea or snack at the nearby dhabas. Betaab Valley (4 km) is the location where the famous movie "Betaab" was filmed. Ponies can be hired to explore the stream and forest, which are bound by many popular trees. The way to Chandanwari from Pahalgam features an idyllic spot for a picnic. Filmgoers will recognize this area instantly, as it has been the location for several movie scenes. The Gulmarg Gondola is a tourist attraction in itself and is one of the highest cable cars in the world. It features a two - stage ropeway: The first stage transfers passengers from the Gulmarg resort at 2, 600 m (8, 530 ft) to Kongdoori Station at 3, 080 m. The second stage of the ropeway, which has 36 cabins and 18 towers, takes skiers to a height of 3, 950 m (12, 959 ft) on Kongdoori Mountain, a shoulder of nearby Apharwat Peak (4, 200 m or 13, 780 ft). Gulmarg also has a famous ski resort and boasts the world's highest 18 - hole golf course.

Activities Description: Today morning after early breakfast, you will drive to visit high altitude lake called as Shonga - tser Lake, popularly known as Madhuri Lake located 35 kms away from Tawang near the China Border. The drive to Sangestser Lake is full of thrill and one can still see the war bankers that had been used during the Chinese aggression in 1962. Nestled amidst the pristine mountains and picturesque surrounding, it was formed in the aftermath of the 1950 earthquake. Prior to the earthquake, this piece of land used to be employed as the grazing ground for the cattle. The evidence of it can be seen in the protruding trunks of the dead trees from the middle of the lake. The lake has been under supervision of Army men, who have also arranged for a cafeteria nearby. Tourists can relish on the delicious Momos, Maggi‟s topped with a cup of tasty coffee or tea. Tourists can also take to trekking around the lake while enjoying the gentle lashes of the pleasant breeze around. You can drive further to Bumla Pass which is located about 37 km away from Tawang at the Indo - China border over 15, 200 ft above sea level. During return take a photo stop at the beautiful PTSO lake Enroute (17 kms away from Tawang, Pangong Tang Tso Lake popularly known as PT Tso which is an extremely scenic drive with bird's eye view of the township below). Later in the afternoon drive back to hotel. Rest of the evening at leisure overnight at hotel

Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan, is popularly known as the "Pink City" due to the pink sandstone used in the construction of buildings in the old walled city. The city owes its name, foundation, and planning to the Great Warrior Astronomer Maharaja Jai Singh II (1699?1744 AD). Founded by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in 1727, Jaipur (City of Victory) is the only city in the world that symbolizes the nine divisions of the Universe through nine rectangular sectors. The architect who formalized the city?s plans based them on the Shilpa Shastra, the epic Hindu treatise on architecture, blending it with the influences of Mughal and Jain architecture of that era. In 1853, the city was painted pink in honor of the visit by Prince Albert. Aside from the busy traffic of bicycles, cars, and buses, little seems to have changed in the city. The afternoon is free for personal exploration or shopping in the colorful and bustling bazaars. Overnight stay at your hotel.

Activities Description: After breakfast, proceed for a full - day city tour of Jaipur. Visit Amer Fort, located 11 km from Jaipur. This fort was the old stronghold of the Kachhwaha clan of Amber and served as the capital until it was moved to Jaipur. The fort is constructed from white marble and red sandstone, and it is even more attractive due to the presence of Maota Lake in the foreground. The fort itself is a beautiful sight, and its clear reflection on the lake creates a dreamlike illusion. An elephant (subject to availability, alternatively by jeep) will spare you the trouble of climbing up to the fortress. Once on top, stroll through the sprawling complex of courtyards and halls with a knowledgeable and articulate guide who will share fascinating tales of the past. Later, visit the City Palace, an overwhelming complex of exquisite palaces, gardens, courtyards, decorative art, and carved doorways. The palace museum houses collections of rare manuscripts, armors, costumes, carpets, and miniature paintings. Walk to the adjacent Jantar Mantar, or Astronomical Observatory, built by the Maharaja of Jaipur in 1726. It is one of five such astronomical wonders created by Sawai Jai Singh and continues to make accurate predictions to this day. Jaipur is a shopper?s paradise, with most bazaars located in the old city offering a wide range of items, from jewelry (precious and semi - precious stones and handcrafted silver) to textiles, handicrafts, and antiques. For avid shoppers, Jaipur is the ideal city to shop and collect memorabilia. Overnight at the hotel.

Activities Description: The Martand Sun Temple sits approximately 7 kilometres northeast of Anantnag on the Mattan plateau - a drive of around 20 minutes from the town centre. The plateau sits at approximately 1, 798 metres above the valley floor and the view from the temple complex across the Kashmir Valley is open in all four directions without obstruction - the Zabarwan hills to the north, the Pir Panjal range to the south, the valley floor stretching to the west. The ruins themselves cover a large rectangular courtyard of carved stone columns with the central shrine base at the centre - 84 subsidiary shrine bases arranged around the inner courtyard wall, the column carving a mix of Aryan and Greco - Roman design elements that reflect both the Karkota dynasty's artistic programme and the trade connections of 8th century Kashmir. This martand temple kashmir package gives the site a full morning - early arrival before the day visitors come from Srinagar is when the plateau silence is at its fullest. The afternoon moves south to Verinag - approximately 30 kilometres from Anantnag, taking around 45 minutes. The Verinag Spring sits at the base of the Pir Panjal in a Mughal garden built by Emperor Jahangir in 1620 - an octagonal stone tank of spring water so clear and deep that the floor is visible from the stone parapet above. Overnight at Anantnag.

Activities Description: The fourth day of your north sikkim tour features an early morning trip to the famous Yumthang valley. Located at an elevation of 11, 800 feet and positioned exactly 140 kilometers from Gangtok, this destination is widely recognized as a paradise for nature lovers. The drive from Lachung takes you through dense forest paths that eventually open up into a massive, flat valley floor surrounded by towering peaks. Set at an elevation of 3575 meters above sea level, the Yumthang Valley is Sikkim's undisputed natural paradise that is easily accessible via road. During the appropriate blooming seasons, you will find that the valley boasts a large variety of Rhododendrons and other delicate alpine flowers. The visual impact of these blooming plants against the backdrop of the rugged mountains provides a fascinating blend of flora and fauna and massive scenic grandeur. You will also visit the Yumthang Tsa - Chu, which is the natural hot spring located on the left bank of the Lachung Chu river. This specific spring is immensely popular among locals and travelers for its believed curative properties and natural healing power. If you wish to extend your geographical exploration, an optional visit to Zero Point or Katao is available for interested guests. Please be fully aware that this specific extension incurs a Zero Point and Katao visit charge extra, pay on spot direct to driver by the guest. These advanced locations bring you even closer to the permanent snowline and the international borders. Whether you choose the extension or remain in the main valley, the natural environment provides a highly satisfying conclusion to your high - altitude touring before the descent begins. Following your comprehensive valley exploration, we initiate the long transfer back to the capital city. The descent takes several hours, requiring our drivers to maintain a safe and consistent speed on the downward slopes. You will complete the day with a direct transfer to your Gangtok hotel for your final overnight stay, transitioning back to the reliable comforts of the urban center. This final night in the capital allows you to enjoy a large dinner and pack your belongings efficiently for the departure scheduled for the next morning.

Activities Description: Arrive at Jodhpur Airport or Railway Station and drive to Jaisalmer. Upon arrival in Jaisalmer, transfer to your hotel. Jaisalmer, a fairy - tale town in the Thar Desert, was founded about 800 years ago by Rawal Jaisal. Unlike any other city, this desert fortress is one of Rajasthan's most exotic and unusual towns. Jaisalmer, an important ancient trading center due to its strategic location on the camel trade routes, is often described as the "Golden City." After lunch, depart for a city tour of Jaisalmer. Visit the famous havelis (mansions) known for their frescoes. The most elaborate and magnificent of all the Jaisalmer havelis is Patwaon Ki Haveli, built by five Jain brothers between 1800 and 1860. Salim Singh Ki Haveli and Nathmal Ki Haveli are the other two havelis that are open to visitors. Built in 1156 by the Bhatti ruler Jaisal, the fort stands atop the 80 - meter high Trikuta Hill. Three walls and 99 bastions surround the fort. Over the centuries, the golden sandstone fortress witnessed many battles between the Bhatti Rajputs, the Mughals, and the Rathores of Jodhpur. Within the fort complex lie beautifully carved Jain temples built between the 12th and 15th centuries. This complex houses priceless ancient manuscripts and other exhibits, including astrological charts and the Jain equivalent of the Christian Shroud of Turin. The afternoon is free for personal exploration or shopping in the colorful and bustling bazaars. Overnight stay at your hotel.

The lake is an idyllic spot for outings. Lodhurva, the ancient capital of the Bhatti clan, is located 16 kilometers from Jaisalmer. Mostly in ruins, it is visited for its great Jain temple, which features exquisite jail work screens, a grand ceiling, and a magnificent triumphal arch at the entrance. Visit Amar Sagar, where the road from Lodhurva to Jaisalmer passes through a grand artificial reservoir for water, a temple, and a promenade along the bank. Kuldhara Village is one of the most interesting places to visit. It is among the 84 villages inhabited by the rich, hard - working Paliwals. The Paliwals deserted their houses overnight, leaving behind a curse that anyone who removed even a stone from the houses would come to grief and perish. Howling winds now rush through the empty streets and the skeletons of houses exposed to the elements remain as remnants of the village. In the evening, proceed for an excursion to Sam Sand Dunes, located 42 kilometers from Jaisalmer. Sam Sand Dunes is the closest point to witness the vast sandy desert and offers an unforgettable experience of camel rides and sunset viewing. Overnight stay at your hotel or camps.

Activities Description: After breakfast, proceed to Jodhpur. Upon arrival, transfer to your hotel. Jodhpur, known as The Blue City, is an oasis in the arid Thar Desert and the second largest city in Rajasthan. This colorful city, adorned with shades of blue, boasts a rich history and a vibrant present that attracts discerning tourists. After lunch, enjoy sightseeing and visit Mehrangarh Fort. This spectacular fort, made from red sandstone, stands on a steep cliff overlooking the skyline of Jodhpur. The foundations of the fort were laid in 1459, and it now houses a museum with an impressive collection of arms, costumes, paintings, and palanquins. Also visit Jaswant Thada, a marble cenotaph built to commemorate Maharaja Jaswant Singh II. The monument is constructed from intricately carved sheets of marble, which are extremely thin and polished, allowing them to emit a warm glow when sunlight dances across their surface. Explore Sardar Bazaar and Clock Tower markets, where you can find vegetables, spices, Indian sweets, textiles, and silver items. These colorful markets feature tiny shops lining narrow lanes, showcasing wood carvings, wrought iron, lacquer work, silver and ivory ornamentation, and leather handicrafts. Overnight stay at your hotel.

We recommend an early start for your morning safari, ideally before sunrise. A team of dedicated and knowledgeable trackers will take you out in customized open 4 - wheel drive jeeps (6 - seater) to find the leopards. You are also likely to spot sloth bears, antelope, and Indian wolves at Jawai Bandh (Dam). Other attractions for bird watchers include migratory birds such as flamingos, geese, and demoiselle cranes. A naturalist accompanies you on every trip to help interpret the exotic flora and fauna of the region. Our trackers come from families who have known the jungle and its animals for generations. The evening is free for personal exploration of the village. Overnight stay at your hotel. Note: Jungle Safari is on a direct payment basis.

Activities Description: After a leisurely breakfast, commence your day with a drive to Kumbhalgarh via Ranakpur. Ranakpur is the largest Jain temple complex in India, dating back to the 15th century. The main temple is dedicated to Adinath, the first Tirthankar. Intricate carvings detail mythological figures, patterns, and motifs on the walls, pillars, and domes. The complex features 1, 444 ornately carved marble pillars, with no two being similar. The beautiful lace - like interiors of the domes exemplify western Indian temple style. Surya Temple and other Jain temples are side attractions. (Temples open only at 12:00 PM. Leather belts, footwear, bare legs, and black clothing are not allowed.) After lunch, drive to Kumbhalgarh, one of the finest examples of defensive fortifications in Rajasthan. The 15th - century fort commands an important strategic position and offers superb views of the surroundings. The 36 km long walls enclose palaces, gardens, temples, and water storage facilities. The fort is believed to have been taken only once in its history. There is also a wildlife sanctuary here, known for wolves, as well as leopards, antelopes, and sloth bears. Visit Kumbhalgarh Fort, the unconquerable fortress is secured under the kind protection of the Aravali ranges. Encircled by thirteen elevated mountain peaks, the fort is constructed on the topmost ridges, around 1, 914 meters above sea level. The fortifications extend to a length of 36 kilometers, making it notable in international records. It is stated to be the second longest wall in the world, the first being the Great Wall of China. The vast complex of the fort includes numerous palaces, temples, and gardens, enhancing its magnificence. Restored, preserved, and protected by The Archaeological Survey of India, the fort is among UNESCO's World Heritage Sites. Also visit Badal Mahal Palace. Enjoy an evening light and sound show at the fort (on a direct payment basis). Overnight stay at your hotel.

The open ocean run is the first part of what makes this day different from anything else in the Andaman Islands - the Port Blair coast disappears behind, the water deepens in colour as the harbour shallows give way to open sea and the crossing gives dolphins a regular appearance alongside the boat on the northeast run, sighted commonly on this route though not guaranteed. Barren Island appears on the horizon as a dark volcanic cone - the approach reveals the black lava coastline where historic flows have reached the water and the caldera rim above. The boat circles the island allowing full views of the volcanic landscape from the water. No landing is permitted on the island. The crater and any visible activity are observed from the boat. Situated 35 km north east of Jomsom, Muktinath temple is dedicated to Lord vishnu. It lies at an altitude of 3750 m and offers a mind blowing Trans Himalayan beauty in the district of Jomsom. The temple of Muktinath is a pagoda shaped temple surrounded by 108 water sprouts and 2 holy ponds.While religious beliefs are the major reason for pilgrims to visit Muktinath temple, it is also remarkably known for the diverse geographical spectrums and wonderful settlement from where you can see the astrounding Himalayan views. Taking a bath in the icy - cold holy pond at Muktinath is believed to wipe off all the sins and liberate. A glimpse of Muktinath is believed to bring good fortune to life and salvation of the soul to get rid of the cycle of birth and rebirth.

Kolsai Lakes are a group of three picturesque alpine lakes located in the Almaty region of Kazakhstan, near the border with Kyrgyzstan. The lakes are part of the Kolsai - Kolderi National Park, which covers an area of about 16, 800 hectares. ? The three lakes are known as Kolsai - 1, Kolsai - 2, and Kolsai - 3, each at a different altitude and offering unique natural beauty. Kolsai - 1 is the lowest lake, situated at an elevation of 1, 818 meters (5, 965 feet) above sea level. Kolsai - 2 is the largest and most picturesque of the three, located at an altitude of 2, 252 meters (7, 388 feet). Kolsai - 3 is the highest lake, nestled at an elevation of 2, 850 meters (9, 350 feet) above sea level. ? The Kolsai Lakes are renowned for their crystal - clear turquoise waters, surrounded by dense coniferous forests, meadows, and snow - capped peaks. The area is rich in biodiversity, with various plant and animal species, including rare and endangered ones. The lakes and their surroundings offer excellent opportunities for hiking, trekking, camping, and photography. ? To visit Kolsai Lakes, you typically need to travel from Almaty, the largest city in Kazakhstan. The journey takes approximately 3 - 4 hours by road, covering a distance of around 330 kilometres (205 miles). It is advisable to arrange transportation beforehand, either by hiring a private vehicle or joining a guided tour. ? It's important to note that due to the pristine nature of the Kolsai Lakes and the national park, there are regulations in place to preserve the environment. Visitors are expected to follow guidelines, such as not littering, not camping in prohibited areas, and respecting the flora and fauna. ? Overall, Kolsai Lakes offer a breathtaking natural retreat for outdoor enthusiasts and nature lovers, providing an opportunity to experience the beauty of Kazakhstan's alpine landscapes. ? Gorky Park features a variety of attractions and amenities including walking paths, playgrounds, sports fields, cafes, restaurants, and a small lake. Siva Gayathri Tours & TravelsBATU CAVES: Siva Gayathri Tours & TravelsBatu Caves, one of Kuala Lumpur's most frequented tourist attractions, is a limestone hill comprising three major caves and a number of smaller ones. Siva Gayathri Tours & TravelsLocated approximately 11 kilometers to the north of Kuala Lumpur, this 100 - year - old temple features idols and statues erected inside the main caves and around it. Siva Gayathri Tours & TravelsIncorporated with interior limestone formations said to be around 400 million years old, the temple is considered an important religious landmark by Hindus. Siva Gayathri Tours & TravelsCathedral Cave - the largest and most popular cavern in Batu Caves - houses several Hindu shrines beneath its 100 - metre - high arched ceiling. Siva Gayathri Tours & TravelsAt the foot of Batu Hill are two other cave temples - the Art Gallery Cave and Museum Cave - which houses numerous Hindu statues and paintings. Activities Description: Otavalo Today we will visit the Quitsato Sundial, a cultural - tourist area located on the equatorial line near the Cayambe volcano, where you will learn about the astronomical knowledge of the region's pre - Hispanic cultures. We will then head to the town of Otavalo, This is truly one of the most interesting towns in Ecuador, where the local Kichwa indigenous culture is not only plainly visible, but on their rise. The town's famous craft market is one of the most visited sites in Ecuador, and with good reason. The market is filled with interesting colorful and sometimes rare objects and crafts. Do remember to bargain, but only if you're interested! The market is held every day on one of the town squares at the foot of the majestic Imbabura Mountain. And to help you navigate the market, you will be given a short explanation of the market and provided with a map of the area. The Local Indian Market has been an economic and social center for more than 4000 years. In the afternoon we'll drive to the Cotacachi - Cayapas Ecological Reserve for a visit to the interpretation center and an outstanding view of the Cuicocha lagoon, a deep - blue crater lake on the lower southern flanks of Cotacachi Volcano. After our hike we will stop at the picturesque colonial town of Cotacachi, famous for its leather work.

Activities Description: Riobamba to Ingapirca to Cuenca After breakfast you will take the scenic drive to Alausi, and the train station for your train ride - Nariz del Diablo Train Journey! The biggest complication faced by the construction of the Trans - Andean railroad was the Devil's Nose, a mountain with almost perpendicular walls. It remains to this day, an impressive piece of engineering. While recovering from the mind - blowing descent you will enjoy the views of the narrow gorge of river Chanchan and will have the chance to learn a bit about the traditions and worldview of the Puruhuas in Sibambe.You now drive south to Ingapirca, an Inca observatory and fortress. This is the most important Inca site in Ecuador, where the Emperor and his entourage would rest during trips to this northern segment of the Empire. After lunch continue to Cuenca Overnight stay at Hotel.

Activities Description: Excursion to Taktshang Monastery After breakfast, drive to the base of the abode of gods and monks, the Taktshang Monastery. Activities Description: Yangon Arrival - Half - day City Tour Greetings from Yangon! The temple city that shimmers. The local guide from Go Myanmar will greet you at the airport today, and you will be taken straight to the city center. For your first taste of the interesting city, you will go on a half - day city tour. Once you pass by the City Hall, Post Office, and High Court, among other historical landmarks with unusual British design, you will first stop at Chauk Htat Gyi Pagoda to see one of the nation's most revered reclining Buddha representations. After leaving the pagoda, proceed to Kandawgyi Lake, the city's most picturesque photo location. Take some time to get images of Karaweik Hall and the Shwedagon Pagoda against this striking backdrop. Finally, visit the Shwedagon Pagoda to complete your city trip. Perched atop a hill, the pagoda commands a view from every angle in the city. Take your time as you meander about the pagoda, taking in the relaxed atmosphere and the people honoring the Buddha.

Activities Description: Kalaw - Heho - Fly to Mandalay - Amarapura - U Bein Bridge Travel to the airport this morning in order to board a trip to Mandalay. Meet your local guide when you arrive, then get ready to see Mandalay's cultural treasures on your honeymoon. Begin the day by paying a first visit to the Mahamuni Pagoda, which is the second most revered Buddhist pagoda in Myanmar after the Shwedagon Pagoda. Every day, villagers attend and pay respect to the immensely renowned golden Buddha picture housed inside the pagoda. Visit local artisan workshops to learn about the products made in the area, such as those that make marble, wood, and gold leaf. The Golden Palace Monastery, renowned for its elaborate woodcarvings and wooden architecture, will be visited after you transfer. Proceed to the Kuthodaw Pagoda, which is renowned for being the largest Buddhist book in the world because it has 729 marble slabs with Buddhist literature carved on them. Enjoy your day by seeing the most photographed sight in Myanmar, the 200 - year - old teak bridge, U Bein Bridge, before the sun sets. Spend the night in Mandalay.

Activities Description: Mandalay - Fly to Bagan - Temples Visit This morning, bid farewell to Mandalay and board a quick flight to Bagan. Discover more about Burmese Buddhist customs and admire the stunning Shwezigon Pagoda, which is the most visited site in Bagan. Visit Ananda Temple, one of Bagan's most enchanting and well - preserved pagodas, to view a wonderful fusion of Mon and North Indian architectural styles. This will be the highlight of your afternoon exploring. You will have the opportunity to pause along the trip in the plains of Bagan in order to take pictures of some of the intriguing nearby temples. Then, we'll go to a nearby lacquerware workshop to observe how the talented craftspeople use age - old techniques to create stunning lacquerware pieces. Drive to the jetty in the late afternoon to board a boat for an Irrawaddy River boat excursion. As you travel down the Irrawaddy River to Shwezigon Pagoda, you may enjoy the amazing sights from a seat in the shade or out on the open deck. Should the weather be sunny today, you will get the opportunity to witness Bagan's breathtaking sunset over the mythical Irrawaddy River. Unwind and take in the view. Spend the night at Bagan.

Activities Description: Bagan - Mt. Popa Enjoy the high point of your journey to Burma by rising early this morning to the sound of birds chirping. To see the breathtaking splendor of Bagan at sunrise, you will fly over its plain in a hot air balloon. There is no better way to take in the splendor of this sprawling 104 square kilometer site of over 3000 temples and shrines than by riding a hot air balloon early in the morning as the sun begins to peek through the clouds. Prepare your camera to get the finest possible picture of the early - morning sight. After the balloon ride, have a little champagne celebration before making the gorgeous journey to Mount Popa, one of the most significant locations in Myanmar's history, culture, and religion. Spend some time hiking the 777 steps to the top of the pagoda, where Taung Kalat, a Buddhist monastery, is located. You can study about the 37 Nats (natural spirits) of Burma within the monastery. After that, we make our way to Popa Mountain Resort, where you will enjoy a private dinner. In Popa Mountain Resort, spend the night.

It was preserved in ruins as a heritage site. A full reconstruction of the Dzong was started in 2016. On a clear day experience a beautiful view of Mt. Jhomolhari (24035 ft.); from here. Then visit the Kichu Lhakhang, one of the oldest Buddhist temples in Bhutan built in 659 AD by the Tibetan King Songtsen Gembo. This is the second of the two temples built in a single day to hold down the giant demoness who was preventing the spread of Buddhism. In the evening, explore the Paro Town. Overnight stay at Paro.

Activities Description: Thimphu Sightseeing (Part - II) After breakfast, visit the Government Post office and make personalized stamps. Post a Card to your friends and families back home. Also visit the Stamp Museum. Then visit the Centenary Farmer's Market (Subject to weekends). After that proceed to the Royal Textile Academy. Interact with weavers in the Textile Academy to see how the traditional Bhutanese fabrics are woven. They also have a a good collection of exclusive and antique Bhutanese textile artifacts. In the afternoon, visit the Drupthob Lhakhang, one of the few surviving nunneries in Bhutan. Then visit the Institute for Zorig Chusum (Institute of thirteen traditional arts and crafts). Students are taught the 13 traditional arts and crafts of Bhutan in this institute. Visit the Institute of Traditional Medicine where medicines are prepared according to the traditional practices. People are also treated here in traditional ways. Finally visit the Jungshi handmade paper factory. The factory manufactures traditional Bhutanese paper using the bark of two tree species, the Daphne tree and Dhekap. The entire process of traditional manufacturing of the handmade paper can be observed. It was previously operated by the government. Now it is run by a private entrepreneur. Overnight stay at Thimphu.

Activities Description: Paro Sightseeing After breakfast start full day sightseeing covering Ta Dzong - Originally built as a watchtower, it is now the National Museum of Bhutan with an excellent collection of Bhutanese antiquities, Rinpung Dzong - consecrated in 1645 by Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal on the site of smaller fort. Currently, it is the administrative seat of Paro district, and also houses the state monastic community of about 200 members. Afternoon, visit the Drukgyel Dzong - Built in 1647 to commemorate the victory over an invasion from Tibet, the dzong was however destroyed by accidental fire in 1951. Then visit the Kichu Lhakhang, one of the oldest Buddhist temples in Bhutan built in 659 AD by the Tibetan King Songtsen Gembo. This is the second of the two temples built in a single day to hold down the giant demoness who was preventing the spread of Buddhism. In the evening, explore the Paro Town. Overnight stay at Paro.

Next, proceed to Chauk Htat Gyi Pagoda, which is the location of a massive statue of a reclining Buddha. This is one of the most venerated Buddha pictures in Myanmar, measuring 66 meters in length. There are traditional symbols etched at the feet of the Buddha, and pilgrims frequently congregate here to pay their respects. After leaving the pagoda, descend to Karaweik Hall Royal, a magnificent golden floating barge on Kandawgyi Lake. Karaweik Hall is regarded as Yangon's most exquisite photo location. Here's your chance to store some amazing pictures. Next, take a drive to the heart of Yangon to see the 2500 - year - old Sule temple, a significant Buddhist temple used for political and religious rituals and thought to contain a strand of the Buddha's hair. We take a picturesque boat ride to Thanlyin in the afternoon, which is a lovely, peaceful town southeast of Yangon. Situated on an island, the Kyaikkauk Pagoda and Kyaikmawwin (Yele) Pagoda are two striking pagodas. For a quick tour, we will first cross the Thanlyin Bridge to arrive at the Kyakikkauk Pagoda. The massive golden Kyakikkauk Pagoda is reminiscent of the Shwedagon Pagoda. After witnessing the locals going about their daily lives in the Kyauktan market, you will board a boat to visit the striking Kyaikmawwun (Yele) Pagoda, which is situated on an island and was constructed in the third century BC by King Zeyasana, the seventh king of the Bagan Dynasty. Later on, head back to Yangon and spend the remainder of the day at leisure.
